‘We Just Are So Gagged’: Jordan Firstman and Reggie Absolom on Club Kid’s Success

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1443 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For his debut feature film, Club Kid, Jordan Firstman envisioned a curly-haired boy who could live in a world of adults.
  • The pair spoke to ELLE about Reggie getting to DJ for the film, whether he’ll have a Radiohead phase, and what the movie says about family.
  • In a recent development, jordan Firstman: I had a very extensive list of things I wanted in the character, and my casting director was like, “You really need to manage your expectations because you’re looking for a child actor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This story contains spoilers for Club Kid.

For his debut feature film, Club Kid, Jordan Firstman envisioned a curly-haired boy who could live in a world of adults. The story was well established by the time casting agent Carmen Cuba met British actor Reggie Absolom, who had appeared in Silo and other series. Firstman, who wrote, directed, and starred in the film, knew he was the perfect one to play Arlo, the 10-year-old son that Firstman’s character Peter never knew he had. Firstman and Absolom grew close rapidly and developed a unique friendship that hasn’t slowed down post-filming. “We text all day,” Firstman notes.

The pair spoke to ELLE about Reggie getting to DJ for the film, whether he’ll have a Radiohead phase, and what the movie says about family.

In a recent development, jordan Firstman: I had a very extensive list of things I wanted in the character, and my casting director was like, “You really need to manage your expectations because you’re looking for a child actor. Baseline, you have to find someone good.” I also just wanted them to be naturally cool and not feel like a child actor [but] feel like a kid. I wanted them to have curly hair. I wanted them to look enough like me that they could be my kid. In the script, the character is written as half Indian, and she was like, “Babe, you’re just not going to find all of that.”.

In a recent development, I found Reggie, and he checked every box. He looked like the kid I had in my head when I wrote it. He also was a really natural actor and nothing felt forced. I sent him a playlist of songs I wrote the movie to, and he told me which ones he liked. I thought he had really good taste, and we just talked for a while and got ice cream. And then it wasn’t until in the process that I found out he was a quarter Indian too. He literally had every single thing that I wanted, and so it did feel like a miracle in a lot of ways.

Reggie Absolom: It was a bit weird at first. But then I became such good friends with everyone anyway and it just felt like I fit in there. It didn’t matter how old I was. I was just friends with everyone, and I was just working like they were as well.

Industry observers note that JF: I love sending people that I love music. Reggie’s music taste influenced the characters. He was into Slipknot at the time, so I wrote a little Slipknot into the script, and he also liked Massive Attack and Cocteau Twins, once I sent him my playlist. I wrote that in.

In a recent development, there’s this whole other component of the actual club music, on which we collaborated so closely with David Peck, who’s in the movie [and who wrote songs for the film and performed them as Heather Asylum]. He did Reggie’s whole DJ set and River Moon consulted. We had real DJs in the scene helping me and making sure we had all the right tracks. The music in the movie is everything; it’s the throughline in the story and the construction of the movie.

In a recent development, RA: It’s from Jordan. Some from David.

JF: Yeah, but most from Jordan.

According to recent reports, RA: You get most of the credit. You gave me quite a few songs, like Cocteau Twins ones and really good Massive Attack ones. I was like, okay, I’m going to go deeper into these and listen to all of their albums. Now there’s some songs that I would’ve never really listened to. When I listened to Cocteau Twins, I would’ve been like, “Okay, this is weird.” But now I’m like, “Okay, maybe I like the weird kind of songs.”.

JF: I think you’re going to also have a major Radiohead era.

RA: Maybe, but I don’t know. I don’t like Radiohead.

It has been revealed that JF: We were going to do “Maybe I’m Amazed” by Paul McCartney, and he wasn’t responding to our emails about licensing it. The day before [we filmed the scene], I was trying to think of other songs, and “Thoroughfare” is my favorite song, I think ever. I feel like I would be that dad that made my kid play Ethel Cain on the piano with me. Then we played it, and it felt really cute and really sincere. We still sang Paul McCartney, but they were like, “You don’t need Paul McCartney. Don’t waste your money.” And “Thoroughfare” is the vibe.

In a recent development, RA: It got me into a lot of different types of music, which I’m happy about. DJing was really fun and something that I’d want to do in the future. Maybe not a full-time job, but something on the side to do, something fun.

JF: Part-time, like Paris Hilton.

RA: It didn’t really influence the roles I wanted to get, but now that I’m in a film that’s done so well, it’s opened up for me to maybe get bigger roles than I would’ve expected before filming this.

RA: The idea of being in a movie, that was the next step for me. I was filming maybe three episodes of a series. I felt like no matter the role, just being in the movie would be the next thing to do. Then the fact that this was a lead role and that I felt similar to Arlo personality-wise in some ways. I felt like I could perform really naturally with the things that Arlo says and the way that he acts.

It has been revealed that JF: Kramer vs. Kramer is such a classic and a movie I love. I often reference An Unmarried Woman with Jill Clayburgh. I love her relationship with her daughter in that movie and how they treat each other like adults. Because Peter has no experience with kids, he doesn’t know how to treat them like anything else but how he treats everyone.

JF: Once I started writing it, I started really understanding Peter and Arlo and what they needed. I actually feel like it’s a gift that they didn’t end up together for both of their lives for that time. That phone call [at the end] is so important, because the door opens again once they’re ready. I think it would’ve been too intense for Peter to [raise Arlo full-time]....He still wasn’t completely out of the party scene. He was still selling drugs. He was not ready to really do this in a real way. Arlo really needed a year of knowing true stability and a normal childhood.

But I think what Peter and his community offered Arlo was a very different version of normal. They encouraged creativity. For a traumatized kid, having an art practice is everything. In my darkest times as a kid, I turned to art. To me, it’s a very human ending, and to me it’s hopeful.

RA: Both of them needed to have that break. They’re trying to find themselves and what they should do. Now, another thing, whilst Arlo was with Peter, he was getting no education really. He tried to get him into school.

RA: He just gave up on that. The ending also leaves it up to interpretation what happens to them in the future. Obviously, it could have been like, oh, they rejoin and they’re father and son forever. I think it’s nicer when the film has an ending that’s up to interpretation a bit, where there could be different branches on the ending.

JF: He really enjoyed fatherhood, so I think he will continue his relationship with Arlo and help him through his teen years and grow up.

According to recent reports, RA: In my opinion, Peter with a baby, adopting a baby would be a bit, like Edison says, “He’s all prepared. Forget the trauma,” or something like that.

Industry observers note that RA: He could do it. He’d need Oscar [Peter’s partner, played by Diego Calva].

It has been revealed that JF: No one involved in this project has had this happen to them. Even Cara [Delevingne] has never been a part of something like this. We just are so gagged. We can’t believe this is happening and that people are responding to it in this way. We get standing ovations everywhere we go, and it’s surreal. We don’t take for granted that this is a rare thing that happens.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Glee has always held a special place in Ryan Murphy’s heart, so when he heard the show was having a major resurgence on social media, it planted the seeds for a reboot in his mind.

It has been revealed that “That show is interesting because it’s come back around,” he mentioned in a July interview with People. “So many young people now watch it. And I’m like, ‘Maybe we should revisit that show.’ My nostalgia and love for that show is enough that I’m like, ‘Well, maybe people would like to see a new incarnation of that in some capacity.’ So yeah, I love that show, and I loved what it became and what it meant to so many people.”.

Months later, Murphy delivered on his comments—on October 21, Disney+ and Hulu granted a series order for Glee, 17 years after the original show’s premiere and 11 years after the final episode. The series also declared the news on its official Instagram, writing, “It’s official. Glee is returning.”.

Details about the reboot are presently sparse, but here’s everything we know so far.

Yes. In September, Murphy told Entertainment Tonight that there has been progress with writing the show. “We have a script. Brad [Falchuk], Ian [Brennan], and I, who wrote all the first two seasons, have written something,” he noted.

Recent findings suggest that the original cast of Glee included Lea Michele, Kevin McHale, Chris Colfer, Darren Criss, Jane Lynch, Amber Riley, Jenna Ushkowitz, Dianna Agron, Heather Morris, Matthew Morrison, Mark Salling, Jonathan Groff, Chord Overstreet, and Harry Shum Jr. Cory Monteith and Naya Rivera were also part of the original cast, but died in 2013 and 2020, respectively.

Sources indicate that while Murphy did not state which stars he has been talking to, he told Entertainment Tonight that he’s “been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members. It’s very sweet, and they all had a lot of questions, but they all were very enthusiastic about the idea.”.

Hours after the reboot news was revealed, Variety reported that Michele will reportedly join the cast of the reboot. “She’s in,” a source told the outlet, while a second source added, “It’s still early-ish days, but it feels good and we’re happy to get the band back together.” Murphy and Michele did not provide a comment.

Following the news, Morris hinted that she’d be stepping back into Brittany S. Pierce’s cheerleading uniform. “Yes ladies and gentle men of women, rumors are true. Brittany S Pierce was in fact lost in the sewers for all these years. But I’m here to inform you that she is alive and well…and back for more #Glee,” she captioned a throwback photo of herself from the set.

While the post feels like a confirmation, Murphy has not confirmed any of the cast members who will return for the show.

According to recent reports, overstreet and McHale also hinted that they’d be returning. Overstreet wrote, “reunited and fit feels so good!” after the reboot news dropped. McHale reacted to a tweet that mentioned Drake has surpassed the Glee cast with the most Billboard Hot 100 chart entries. “Challenge accepted,” he replied to the tweet.

On October 23, Deadline offered an update on Morris’s and Overstreet’s statuses. The outlet reported that they were in talks to join the reboot.

During his November 11 appearance on The Daily Beast’s Obsessed podcast, Colfer revealed that he’s planning to have more “conversations” about potentially joining the reboot.

He added, “It was really hard going back to the show after Cory passed, and I’m sure it’d be really difficult, especially now that Naya’s gone too,” Colfer noted. “But I guess you have to think, are you going to let the loss of two people you love very much prevent you from being around a dozen other people you love as well? There’s a lot to think about with it.”.

Colfer does have ideas on what his character, Kurt Hummel, would be up to in the current timeline, though. “I would love to see him like a Miranda Priestly-type, running his own fashion blog or a magazine,” he shared. “I could also see him on tour with Chappell Roan, styling her. There’s a lot of fun avenues they could explore.”.

Over the years, several cast members have shared their reactions to a potential Glee reboot, with some stating they would not return to the series if it were made.

Recent findings suggest that michele, who played the show’s central main character, Rachel Berry, told E! News in September that she’d be open to following Murphy if he expanded the Glee universe. “I love Glee, I will always love Glee,” she noted. “I love Ryan Murphy; it holds such a special place in my heart for me, so I will follow Ryan wherever he goes.”.

Colfer told Bustle in an interview earlier this month that Glee “was a really tough show to do, and it would be really hard to do it now that Naya [Rivera] is gone.” He added, “I do know that Glee fans would probably come after me with pitchforks and jazz hands if I said no.”.

Lynch reflected on her Glee character, Sue Sylvester, in an interview with Entertainment Tonight earlier this month and confirmed that she would join the cast again in a heartbeat. “I would be in like that,” she noted.

In May 2025, Riley, who starred as Mercedes Jones, mentioned that she wouldn’t be interested in returning to Glee during her appearance on Monét X Change’s Monét Talks podcast.

Recent findings suggest that “I just feel like what we did was so phenomenal, I don’t want to risk trying to reinvent the wheel,” she mentioned. “Now if they redo it, I think that’s amazing, because there are so many kids now that are just now discovering Glee, and so I think that that’d be really dope. But, you know, we lost cast members. I just feel like the chemistry, that formula, was so specific, and it’s changed now, so I don't know if it would be as effective. I’m always prepared for that question.”.

Morris (Brittany S. Pierce) shared in a 2024 interview that she would be down to join the reboot if it were made. “I would,” she stated in a video interview. “I think the film industry has come a long way. It was a really tough show to do, and I think being in the space that I’m [in] now, absolutely. I yearn so bad to be in a musical again.”.

In 2023, Criss (Blaine Anderson) discussed a potential reboot and revealed that he would be on the fence about it.

“I’m not against it. I know people would like that. I think what made Glee so special is where it sat in its specific time and place,” he explained during his PeopleCon appearance. “I think a lot of cultural moments are defined by the alchemy of where we’re at as a society, and the way it called and responded to each other made it really special.”.

Criss continued, “While I, as a fan of Glee, would go, ‘Yeah, I would love to see more,’ I do think there’s something we have to remember about the why, when, and how [the show was] special being very specific to one time. I wouldn’t be against it, but I’m also not screaming to do it. I’m somewhere in between. They have to make it really count.”.

At AdoptTogether’s annual Los Angeles Baby Ball in 2022, Ushkowitz (Tina Cohen-Chang) told E! News that she would be open to a reboot if the right team worked together to bring it to life.

Industry observers note that “If Ryan was doing it and the right people were involved,” she told the outlet at the time. “I would consider it.” She also dispelled rumors of drama between members of the cast, adding, “We’re a family—families don’t always have to get along. When we were working together, it took more energy to fight than it did to just get along. I spent more hours with them than literally, my own family.”.

The colored tights renaissance was alive and well on the fall 2026 runways, with Chanel, Marc Jacobs, and Valentino leading the charge.

#7590. Is The Rings of Power Still Worth Watching?

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (955 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Is The Rings of Power Still Worth Watching?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when I was a kid, I was obsessed with something called Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog.
  • However unfair, it’s through that spectrum of two extreme ends that I see fantasy television like The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power.
  • We’re four years and three seasons (lol) into The Rings of Power’s planned five seasons on Prime Video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when I was a kid, I was obsessed with something called Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog. If you weren’t a first-grader in 1998, it was a Fox Kids Saturday morning series about four heroes in medieval Ireland who morphed into armored knights to battle dragons and evil witches. It was Power Rangers by way of Celtic mythology, and it kicked ass. I was a wee bit too young for Hercules and Xena then, and Mystic Knights made sword-and-sorcery stories accessible to my Saturday morning-addled brain. Two years after it went off the air, The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring stormed into theaters.

However unfair, it’s through that spectrum of two extreme ends that I see fantasy television like The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power. I have a standard through which I see this genre in this particular medium. On the big screen, fantasy can feel endless, its scope stretching beyond the horizon. On the small screen, you can feel the ceiling over everyone’s heads. Even Game of Thrones had a coffee cup slip through the veil. Which is why, despite the distant relation to Peter Jackson’s immaculate movies, The Rings of Power is quintessential fantasy TV on par with Mystic Knights. That’s not a bad thing—it’s just perspective.

We’re four years and three seasons (lol) into The Rings of Power’s planned five seasons on Prime Video. After all this time, it still hasn’t won over skeptics. There are long and boring reasons why Tolkien faithful have been averse to the prequel show. They have complaints about pacing, plotting, creative liberties from Tolkien’s textbooks of lore, and general execution. Regrettably, they more often than not get mixed up with old-fashioned racism and misogyny. (Valar forbid a dwarf be a Black woman.) But sometimes the worst people you know have a point: The Rings of Power has been an underwhelming experience. Despite its strong start in season 1, the show simply hasn’t escaped the long, long shadow of Jackson’s cinematic trilogy. (Even Jackson never lived up to his own standards. See: The Hobbit.).

Sources indicate that amid the show’s large ensemble, the series bet many of its chips on Charlie Vickers as Sauron. Though handsome, Vickers’ lack of charisma, middling scriptwriting for his role, and a severe lack of sexual tension with co-star Morfydd Clark (as Galadriel) have sadly made Rings of Power somnambulant. Now in season 3, the chance to course-correct is long past, and the rigor mortis of its missteps have now settled in.

Recent findings suggest that season 1 had a strong start. Sauron is a hottie, and his early relationship to Galadriel carried with it an air of intrigue and yearning until his mask came off. Maybe there could have been a whole show about their forbidden attraction. (Some fans have already coined “Saurondriel.”) The good girl/bad boy pairing is a tried and true tradition, with a subset of the Star Wars fandom possessing a bizarre obsession with Daisy Ridley’s Rey getting it on with Adam Driver’s Kylo Ren. Who are any of us to deny ourselves this pleasure?

Industry observers note that but season 2 didn’t seize on nor improve what was its grace. Their characters were kept separate until the finale, where they reunited on the battlefield. It’s a good scene, to be fair, it’s just maddening that what could have been the whole show was just five minutes, including a bloodless sword fight.

Now here we are in season 3, and it’s more of the same. All of the characters are on a journey across Middle-earth, the story is moving along at a steady, if at times meandering pace, Sauron is quite literally plotting everything from his high tower, and there is a clear endpoint at the end of it all: the forging of the One Ring. As of this writing, the season’s four episodes (available to stream now) suggest we’ll get there in due time. There have been some big-name casualties already, and some impressive set pieces that actually feel like things are intensifying at the right temperatures.

Still, this is Lord of the Rings we’re talking about here. For all the lore and imagination Tolkien spilled onto his pages, his was a story still mired in the age-old tradition of good versus evil. That is Rings of Power too, where even morality comes in shades of stark black and white (mostly) and just enough polished VFX and production design to sell the immersion. One could ask, “What more do you want?” Somehow, it’s still not really enough. Even now, there is still too little energy, too little thrust, too little verve—and yes, still too little sex appeal—to warrant undivided attention. The Rings of Power is mighty pretty to look at on a massive 50-inch LED screen. (I’m particularly engrossed anytime we follow Daniel Weyman’s Gandalf, who is always strolling through the most picturesque backdrops.) But it’s also far too easy to get distracted by more exciting things, like your laundry machine timer going off. In other words: The Rings of Power is a television show.

For all the money Jeff Bezos spent on making Rings of Power a reality, it’s still just TV. It’s maybe a cruel, cosmic, and frankly righteous joke that the billionaire’s very clear marching orders to his team—“I want my Game of Thrones,” is how he was quoted—have resulted in precisely that. A fantasy television series. Blame the streaming era for pigeonholing everything of this caliber into a blockbuster with lofty expectations. Not all TV should be appointment viewing. Sometimes a TV show can and should just be what it is: Mystic Knights, with a few extra zeroes.

#7589. Tech Report: Nanofat Is Dermatologists’ Best-Kept Secret for Younger, Fresher Skin

📖 Baca

Tech Report: Nanofat Is Dermatologists’ Best-Kept Secret for Younger, Fresher Skin

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (914 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the last few years have been unkind to our facial fat.
  • Industry observers note that “Adipose tissue is a rich source of growth factors and progenitor cells, and re-injecting fat is probably one of the best ways to regenerate the full potential of healthy skin I've seen in the last decades,” claims Patricia Ogilvie, a Munich-based dermatologist and member of the Dior Reverse Aging Board.
  • Recent findings suggest that you’re probably familiar with fat transfer, a procedure that’s been around for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the last few years have been unkind to our facial fat. We sliced out our buccal pads to create sunken-in, razor-sharp cheekbones. We zapped our skin with thermal devices that accidentally melted fat away in pursuit of boosting collagen. We injected our stomachs with fat-loss GLP-1 medications, leaving our faces looking hollow. Droopy. Structurally unsound. As it turns out, facial fat is critical infrastructure—not just for looking younger, but for your skin's overall health and quality. And while you can’t choose where you lose or gain fat, you can choose to have a doctor siphon it, remix it, and reinject it.

Industry observers note that “Adipose tissue is a rich source of growth factors and progenitor cells, and re-injecting fat is probably one of the best ways to regenerate the full potential of healthy skin I've seen in the last decades,” claims Patricia Ogilvie, a Munich-based dermatologist and member of the Dior Reverse Aging Board. “There are trends that are not really worth being a trend. I think the restaging of the importance of adipose tissue is very justified.”.

Recent findings suggest that you’re probably familiar with fat transfer, a procedure that’s been around for decades. In simple terms, fat transfer takes adipose tissue from one area of your body, like your flanks, liposuctions it, and moves it to another area, like your breasts or cheekbones. “With traditional fat transfer, it’s about restoring volume. And because it’s your own living tissue, it can integrate beautifully and give you very natural-looking results,” says dermatologist Sheerene Idriss, medical director and founder of Idriss Dermatology in New York City. “But what’s interesting is that fat isn’t just fat. It also contains regenerative cells, including adipose-derived stem cells, and growth factors that may help improve the surrounding tissue over time. Nanofat is where it gets really exciting.”.

Recent findings suggest that nanofat is part of a latest class of regenerative aesthetics offered by dermatologists and plastic surgeons, treatments that don’t just make you look better, but rather address the signs of aging from the inside out by stimulating collagen or repairing tissue. Imagine taking that same fat from a traditional fat transfer and processing it into a fine, milky liquid rich in your own stem cells and growth factors, then injecting or microneedling it back into your face—that’s nanofat.

“Instead of using it to restore volume, you’re using it to potentially improve skin quality itself,” notes Idriss. “These cells and growth factors communicate with surrounding tissue and can stimulate processes involved in collagen production, tissue repair, and blood vessel formation. So you’re not just trying to fill a wrinkle. You’re trying to improve the skin itself—its thickness, resilience, and texture—so that wrinkle potentially becomes less noticeable.”.

Industry observers note that the best areas for nanofat injections include under the eye, a notoriously risky area for hyaluronic acid fillers, and the cheekbones. “The ideal patient for nanofat is someone who's starting to notice thinner, crepier skin, fine lines, or changes in skin texture, especially around the eyes, neck, or chest, and wants to improve skin quality rather than add volume,” adds Idriss, who both has had the treatment done and offers it in her practice. Plus, Ogilvie notes, nanofat doesn’t attract water the way fillers do, so it won’t cause under-eye puffiness (a common post-filler complaint). But because nanofat doesn’t restore volume as much as it reinvigorates your skin, you can inject it almost anywhere you’re noticing signs of aging.

“We do it under tumescent local anesthesia, so you’re awake the entire time, and recovery is usually pretty quick,” states Idriss. “I personally had nanofat and fat transfer in June and was back at work the next day. The biggest downside is some soreness at the fat extraction site, which usually lasts a few days, and you’ll want to avoid strenuous exercise for about a week. Because there’s no general anesthesia, you’re also avoiding the grogginess and recovery associated with being put under.”.

Like any cosmetic treatment, it has risks and downsides. Experts note that nanofat isn’t the right treatment for anyone looking to restore significant volume loss or seeking instant results. “Improvement in skin quality can vary from person to person, and it takes months to see the full results,” Idriss adds. “There are rare but serious risks, including infection, vascular complications, and even vision loss when injecting certain areas of the face.” But patients who have tried the procedure say the recovery is quick and easy, with results compounding over weeks, though they ultimately fade away faster than traditional injectables.

Nanofat injections sit somewhere between microfat and hyaluronic acid fillers. Microfat can be lumpy and unpredictable when injected, sometimes leading to lopsided results. Plus, in any fat transfer, only a small amount of fat survives. Fillers, on the other hand, offer long-lasting precision and volume restoration, but patients are tired of looking overfilled and unnaturally plump. Nanofat helps your skin look naturally healthier, fresher, and firmer, at least for a while. After all, it’s made from you.

Industry observers note that “I look at this as something you can do periodically throughout your life, but what you do in between treatments is just as crucial. And that’s why I don’t believe in demonizing any one treatment, including filler,” says Idriss. “When used appropriately, for the right indication, these treatments can all work beautifully together. It’s about knowing what you need, when you need it, and when enough is enough.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, now that the Halloween candy bowls are empty, you might find thoughts of tinsel, garland, and fairy lights dancing in your head, but is it really time to trade your pumpkins for holiday trimmings?
  • Industry observers note that if you belong to a Homeowners’ Association (and over 78.1 million Americans do), the question of when to put up your outdoor décor may be dictated by their guidelines.
  • If you don’t live in an HOA, you may not get fined for decorating too early, but you will get judged by neighbors who find pre-Thanksgiving holiday displays a little, well, tacky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, now that the Halloween candy bowls are empty, you might find thoughts of tinsel, garland, and fairy lights dancing in your head, but is it really time to trade your pumpkins for holiday trimmings? Some have strong opinions on the topic, half believing the jolly spirit of the holiday season doesn't start until after Thanksgiving, the other rushing to unbox their silver bells as soon as the clock strikes 12 on November 1—but the choice isn’t always yours to make.

Industry observers note that if you belong to a Homeowners’ Association (and over 78.1 million Americans do), the question of when to put up your outdoor décor may be dictated by their guidelines. HOAs tend to have rules about holiday decorations, restrictions covering their location (within the boundaries of your yard, of course), sound level (not too loud), safety (no open flames), light color, and when the decorations can be installed. In some communities, you can even be fined for bringing out the twinkle lights and nativity creche before Thanksgiving—this happened to one Florida man in 2002, when he was hit with a fine of $1,000 for putting his lights up on November 6.

If you don’t live in an HOA, you may not get fined for decorating too early, but you will get judged by neighbors who find pre-Thanksgiving holiday displays a little, well, tacky. To be fair, holding until after Thanksgiving does have its perks—why would you pass on the opportunity to decorate a gorgeous fall tablescape? In the spirit of peace on earth and goodwill toward man, we asked design experts what to do. Here’s what they mentioned.

Additional copy by Meghan Shouse and Alyssa Khan.

In a recent development, you might follow a religious tradition that guides your holiday decorating, like placing the Baby Jesus in the nativity on Christmas Day or keeping the tree up until Epiphany. But when it comes to secular etiquette, there are no hard-and-fast rules about when to start (or stop) decking the halls.

“Most people find it tasteful to stick within the weeks or the month of the holiday itself,” points out Lizzie Post, co-president of The Emily Post Institute and author of Emily Post’s Etiquette—The Centennial Edition. “That stated, there is no etiquette that dictates it. It’s the same way you can paint your house neon orange with blue stripes—there’s nothing that says you can’t. It’s really, do you want to be the person who does?”.

Recent findings suggest that for designer Tan France, the answer to that question is decidedly yes. For the past decade, he and his husband have been decorating their tree on Halloween and taking it down on Valentine’s Day. “I’m British, and we don’t really do Halloween,” he explains. “When I moved here 16 years ago, I was more obsessed with Christmas. So on Halloween day, when everyone else is crafting their costumes, I want to be decorating the tree. And a tree brings my husband and me a lot of joy when we come down and turn the lights on first thing in the morning. It’s just a lovely thing to perk your day up.”.

Do people question France about his decision to put up decorations so early, and for so long? “Oh gosh, yeah, everyone asks that,” he indicates. “Online, the press, neighbors. And my answer is really simple: Why delay joy?”.

Recent findings suggest that if you are jonesing to do some holiday decorating, there's good news: While Christmas might be weeks away, there is one happening right now. It’s called Thanksgiving.

In a recent development, “Anytime before midnight of Thanksgiving is too early to decorate,” insists Wendy Kerrigan, founder of Atelier Design in Newly introduced Orleans. “Filling the house with Christmas decorations too soon really takes away from the beauty of Thanksgiving, moving your mind into the bustle of Christmas.”.

Kerrigan wishes more people would celebrate the fall season for longer; rushing to the tinsel takes away from the beauty of the autumn season, “Thanksgiving can be experienced in a special way too, filling the house with fall colors, fall leaves, gourds, and cornucopia,” indicates Kerrigan. “Instead of trying to hurry the year along, enjoy each family celebration for what it is.”.

Sources indicate that even more, sprinting to the Yuletide season robs the holiday of its own magic. “What makes things special when they’re once a year is that they’re experiences you look forward to,” states Vermont-based interior designer Joshua Smith. “How many holidays can we take at one time? Are we doing Black Friday in July now? Let’s just enjoy the season that we’re in!”.

Industry observers note that when it comes to holiday decorating, many hands make light work. Several designers say they take advantage of the long holiday weekend and enforced family time to rope in some extra help making spirits bright. “In my parents' home, we start decorating right after Thanksgiving dinner. It’s a rare opportunity for everyone to be together, and my siblings and I stay to help out our parents,” notes Fresh York-based designer Mikel Welch. “Plus, it’s a much better tradition than terrorizing sales associates on Black Friday Eve!".

Industry observers note that smith has a plan for bringing the Christmas spirit to his home, without shouldering the burden of doing all the hall-decking himself. Last year, his family decorated their trees over Thanksgiving weekend and made it a tree-decorating contest. With his husband's family in town, “they’ll be divided into three teams, decorating three trees, and I’ll go around at the end judging, and everyone will win prizes. We’re not all going to be together at Christmas, so this activity is a fun way to celebrate the season and not do all the work myself,” he notes.

Still, early decorators would argue that the amount of effort needed to set up holiday decor is another reason to put up decorations early—and keep them up late. “This is the most miserable time of the year; it gets dark so early, it’s so darn cold. I just think you should do everything you can to bring yourself joy,” claims France. “Why put in all that effort for a few weeks?”.

Even those who are normally on the side of waiting to decorate agree that desperate times call for dopamine decorating. Whether it’s the state of your inbox or the state of the world that is stressing you out, if you’re feeling a little blue, go right ahead and pull out the red and green.

In a recent development, “In a perfect calendar, the day after Thanksgiving would be my official start to the holiday season—it's traditionally the day when my family goes out into the woods of Tahoe National Forest to chop down our tree, drag it home, and decorate it,” says designer Noz Nozawa of Noz Design. “But this year, the day after Halloween is when I let the holidays start—there's plenty to worry about, and having my nutcrackers and string lights out a few weeks early can only boost spirits.”.

Whenever you decorate, it can be a way to bring fun to a not-always joyful world. “We have no control over a lot of things in our lives, but when we walk through the door of our home, we choose to focus our energy and attention on whether that is on fear or on love and joy,” claims Smith. “And this holiday season, I think more than ever we have to focus on ways to bring more light to ourselves and to each other.”.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to early decor, “I can handle it from my neighbor; I cannot handle it from a corporation,” notes Post. That may be because we know the Christmas displays popping up in a big-box store alongside the Halloween candy are trying to sell us something, while a neighbor decorating is spreading joy, spending their own time and money to brighten the dark winter nights. For a shop, holiday decorating is mercenary. For an individual, it’s a mitzvah.

Sources indicate that if you appreciate the joy inspired by holiday displays and do want to start setting them up early or keep them up late, consider finding a middle ground by leaning toward decor that’s more about lighting up the night, rather than marking a particular occasion. “I see a lot of people in Vermont leaving the actual lights up, not so much like blow-up Santas or things like that, but the actual lights up for the entire winter,” says Post.

According to recent reports, if you’re a minimalist (or live in a studio apartment), you don’t need a tree to decorate. “If you don’t have a tree, I’m going to invite you to place a hurricane lamp on your coffee table with a wreath of greenery around it and light a candle in the evening,” says Smith. “Because what we know from neuroscience and neuroaesthetics is, you’ve got to engage the senses to nourish the soul!” Light a candle or turn on some twinkle lights, and you’re liable to spark joy as well.

It has been revealed that france would argue that even his trees aren’t occasion-specific. “Here’s the thing: I’m Muslim, and my tree and the lights on our house aren’t necessarily for Christmas,” he explains. “It’s to celebrate Thanksgiving, Christmas, and the New Year. This is the most miserable time of the year. It gets dark so early, it gets light so late, it’s so darn cold. I just think do everything you can to bring yourself joy.”.

According to recent reports, though you’d never find them rushing to hang their stockings, the designer duo behind the Kansas City-based firm Kobel + Co, Elizabeth Bennett and Mallory Robins, say there’s one design scheme you can always tap into if you find yourself in the class of outliers running to get decor up before Christmas Eve. “Ralph Lauren Holiday isn't just having a moment; it's a classic holiday go-to for so many reasons,” Bennett explains. “Warm crimsons, rich browns, tactile fabrics, and blue-green plaids make a beautiful holiday palette. Layer in antique silver pieces and simple glass ornaments. A little patina and variation keep everything from feeling too matched. The goal is a warm, welcoming home with pieces that feel collected and personal.” After all, you want it to feel like home, even at Christmas.

The 11 Best Makeup Brush Sets, According to Experts

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, crafting the perfect smoky eye or no-makeup-makeup finish isn’t always easy, no matter how many TikTok tutorials you’ve watched.
  • Even the most talented artists need the right tools to get the best results, which is why we’ve consulted professionals like Anisa Telwar Kaicker, founder of Anisa Beauty, and professional makeup artist and master esthetician Nicole Erickson for their top picks.
  • Whether you’re a budding professional, a total beginner, or just looking to upgrade your beauty routine, we’ve included some of the best makeup brush sets below that might actually make you want to clean your tools after each use.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, crafting the perfect smoky eye or no-makeup-makeup finish isn’t always easy, no matter how many TikTok tutorials you’ve watched. But beyond having the skills to pull off a glamorous beauty look, using one of the best makeup brush sets can make all the difference in your concealer placement, blush intensity, and more.

Even the most talented artists need the right tools to get the best results, which is why we’ve consulted professionals like Anisa Telwar Kaicker, founder of Anisa Beauty, and professional makeup artist and master esthetician Nicole Erickson for their top picks.

Whether you’re a budding professional, a total beginner, or just looking to upgrade your beauty routine, we’ve included some of the best makeup brush sets below that might actually make you want to clean your tools after each use. Plus, experts share tips on choosing the best makeup brush set for your skill level and preferred makeup looks, and weigh in on the natural-versus-synthetic bristle debate.

Recent findings suggest that whether you opt for no-makeup makeup or go a little bolder, this well-rounded set from Sigma Beauty’s cosmetics experts has you covered. It includes tools for foundation, concealer, and powder, plus a mix of large and small angled options (and a couple of eye-specific brushes) to complete your next look seamlessly.

Brushes included: F30 Large powder, F50 duo fibre, F40 large angled contour, F60 foundation, F50 concealer, E40 tapered blending, E60 large shader, E55 eye shading, E70 medium angled shading, E30 pencil, E65 small angle, E05 eyeliner.

Skip unnecessary price markups and grab this complete 14-piece set from BS-MALL, a cosmetics tool manufacturer that produces makeup brushes for many big-name beauty brands. This Amazon reviewer favorite includes face and eye brushes in various shapes and sizes, making it ideal for those looking to build skills and try upcoming products or application methods without a major financial commitment.

Type of brushes included: Angled face brush, flat face brush, flat angled face brush, round face brush, tapered face brush, eyeshadow brush, angled eyeshadow brush, concealer brush, spoolie, lip brush, eyeliner brush, precision eyeliner brush, dual-ended brow and eyeliner brush.

According to recent reports, celebrity makeup artist and Makeup by Mario founder Mario Dedivanovic just dropped this trio of dual-ended face and eye brushes, and Bazaar editors couldn’t be more excited to put them to use. The limited edition bundle is highly versatile, and nicely includes a carrying pouch for easy transport.

Type of brushes included: F3 dual-ended Precision Powder brush, F4 dual-ended Foundation and Face brush, E6 dual-ended Eyeshadow brush.

Upcoming to makeup application? This five-piece brush set from makeup artist Laura Geller is designed to streamline your routine, not complicate it. The standout is the retractable kabuki brush, which buffs powder, cream, or liquid foundation for a diffused, airbrushed look. Plus, its retractable design helps minimize messes in your makeup bag. The set also includes two eyeshadow brushes—one for all-over color and another for creating smoky eyes—an angled brush for blush and bronzer, and a large, fluffy brush for adding a soft, bronzed glow to the high points of your face.

Type of brushes included: Retractable kabuki brush, angled blush brush, face brush, all-over eyeshadow brush, blending crease brush.

In a recent development, dirty makeup brushes can harbor breakout-causing bacteria, so Morphe upgraded its popular makeup brush sets with antibacterial synthetic bristles. While you’ll still need to wash your tools regularly, the silver-ion-infused material will put your mind at ease during day-to-day use. Suitable for beginners and experts alike, this eight-piece kit is a great choice for anyone looking for a fresh start.

Brushes included: M104 Domed foundation brush, M133 domed concealer brush, M161 large rounded powder brush, M204 rounded blush brush, M303 large paddle packer eyeshadow brush, M332 medium rounded blender eyeshadow brush, M383 pointed detail eye brush, M401 dual-ended angled brow brush and spoolie.

In a recent development, if you’re after the essentials, grab this six-piece Real Techniques set for just $20. More than 40,000 five-star Amazon reviewers say these budget-friendly brushes are versatile enough for most everyday makeup looks and durable enough to withstand years of daily use.

According to recent reports, “You don’t necessarily need to buy the most expensive set on the market,” Erickson notes. “Affordable makeup brush brands like Real Techniques and Eco Tools are sufficient for those wanting to keep it simple. Assess what you’re doing makeup-wise daily and consider what you actually need.”.

Number of brushes: Four (plus two makeup sponges).

Types of brushes included: RT 400 blush brush, RT 300 deluxe crease brush, RT 402 setting brush, RT 200 expert face brush.

Another great option for beginners, this budget-friendly set includes the basic face and eye brushes you need to apply go-to products like concealer, blush, and eyeshadow—without overwhelming you with options for blending and detailing.

It has been revealed that erickson also points out that many beauty products don’t require brushes at all. “If you’re a minimalist, there are quite a few cream-based face products and even eyeshadows you can apply with your fingers. Using your fingers can also help to warm up and blend the product—just make sure your hands are clean.”.

Brushes included: Full face blush brush, angled foundation face brush, blurring concealer brush, defined crease eye brush, angled liner eye brush.

Sources indicate that if you’re the type to do your makeup in the gym locker room or during your morning commute, try this travel-friendly brush set from Hourglass Cosmetics. This seven-piece assortment includes cult-favorite tools you’ve likely seen on TikTok, including the brand’s dual-ended Ambient Lighting Edit Brush, all housed in a luxe vegan leather roll.

Types of brushes included: Vanish seamless finish foundation brush, vanish seamless finish concealer brush, veil single powder brush, ambient lighting edit brush, N° 6 tapered blender brush, N° 12 beveled shadow brush, N° 14 detail setting brush.

According to recent reports, if you’re a fan of Saie’s makeup essentials, we bet you’ll love applying them with this brand’s six-piece brush set. Three brushes in varying sizes and textures help you create a natural-looking base with your preferred liquid, cream, and powder complexion products. Then, you can go in with the dual-ended brush for highlighter, concealer or bronzer, add a rosy flush with the powder blush brush, and finish with your favorite setting powder using the all-over powder brush.

Brushes included: Base brush, fluffy brush, substantial brush, double brush.

Thoughtfully designed ergonomic handles make these Guide Beauty brushes a great choice for everyone, including makeup lovers with limited mobility. Rest the brand’s signature Guide Ring between your fingers and place your thumb on the pad for a comfortable grip that gives you total control, even if you struggle with shaky hands.

Brushes included: All-over eyeshadow brush, blend & crease brush, define & smudge brush.

If your current face makeup brushes aren’t cutting it, upgrade to this do-it-all duo from Anisa Beauty. The larger brush, the brand’s cult-favorite Pinnacle Foundation Brush, features angled bristles that curve to your face contours, blending liquid foundation, cream blush, and bronzer effortlessly. The compact concealer brush fits perfectly under the eyes for a smooth, crease-free finish.

Sources indicate that “This set of brushes from Anisa Beauty makes applying my base makeup a dream,” beauty commerce editor Tiffany Dodson Davis says. “Not only are the bristles super soft, but their angled shapes make it easy to blend my foundation and concealer rapidly and seamlessly.”.

Brushes included: Pinnacle foundation brush, angled concealer brush.

What Are the Best Makeup Brushes Worth Shopping?

It has been revealed that according to Erickson, the most essential makeup brushes in your set are the ones you use with powder products, such as bronzer, blush, or setting powder. "Everyone should own a small powder brush—or even something that resembles a large eyeshadow brush—to cut shine where needed and set concealer. An angled brush can be helpful when using bronzer or contour, as well as a medium-sized cheek brush for powder blush.".

And when it comes to eye makeup brushes, the expert adds, "It can be helpful to have a dual-sided angled brush-spoolie combo for brows, as well as for winged liner. A small, dense, pointed brush for the lash line and inner corner is nice to have, as well as one or two blending brushes for the eyelids.".

Should I Opt for Synthetic or Natural Bristles?

Sources indicate that "I like to say there is nothing 'natural' about animal hair," Anisa Telwar Kaicker tells Bazaar. "It can dry faster and break more quickly. Man-made synthetics can be long-lasting, hygienic, innovative in shape, and soft to the touch.".

Erickson agrees that synthetic makeup brushes outperform products made using animal by-products. "Synthetic brushes tend to be more durable and last longer. Less and less natural bristles areused today, and as a makeup artist, I don’t think we need them, performance-wise.".

What’s the Most Effective Way to Clean Makeup Brushes?

Recent findings suggest that "When I deep clean my makeup brushes once or twice a month, I typically use Dr. Bronner’s 18-in-1 castile soap," Erickson notes. "At the very least, use a quick-dry brush cleaner like Sephora’s Daily Brush Cleaner between each use to avoid the spread of bacteria.".

Telwar Kaicker suggests that after deep cleaning, you remove excess water from your brushes with a towel. Then, tilt the brush downward to prevent water from seeping into the ferrule and breaking down the glue in the brush head.

How Often Should I Replace My Makeup Brushes?

According to Erickson, high-quality, well-cared-for brushes can last for years. "If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it. I’ve had some of my makeup brushes last a decade and some only last a year or two. If you love it and you’re able to properly sanitize it, use it for as long as you can.".

Sources indicate that how do you know when it's time for a new set? Erickson claims it all comes down to the glue. "Typically, when a makeup brush goes bad, the glue between the brush and handle starts to break down due to wear and moisture from cleaning. When that happens, toss it and move on. For beauty blenders and sponges that harbor bacteria, toss them after a few uses, no matter how well you sanitize them. Toss after a few uses, especially if you’re acne-prone.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the seventh annual Kips Bay Decorator Show House in Dallas returns to 2999 Turtle Creek Boulevard, but don’t expect it to look anything like it did in 2025. A new group of the country’s leading designers has taken on the 25,000-square-foot French Renaissance estate, transforming each room to showcase bold ideas, highlight exceptional craftsmanship, and reveal the upcoming trends we can expect to see in the world of interior design.

Visit the show house and see each of the 22 designers’ rooms, from the first dedicated home gym in Kips Bay history by Dallas-based Platinum Gym Design, to a small but mighty European-inspired kitchen by Stephenson Home, to a 1970s-inspired primary bathroom fit with a glass brick shower and curtained-off water closet by Nuance Interiors. With sponsors like Benjamin Moore, The Shade Store, The Rug Tech giant, and more, the vibrant and personality-filled spaces come as no surprise.

As always, proceeds from the show house go to the Kips Bay Boys & Girls Club, which provides educational, enrichment, and developmental programs to thousands of young people, as well as Dallas-based nonprofits Dwell with Dignity and The Crystal Charity Ball.

To see this celebration of exceptional design, you can purchase tickets here and visit the house from Saturday, November 14th to Sunday, December 6th. However, if you can’t make it to the Lone Star State in time, check out some of our favorite moments from the event below.

According to recent reports, kelsi Lamberth of Nuance Interiors pulled inspiration from the 1970s for her primary bathroom, separating the shower from the main prep space using a curved glass brick wall. The sculptural aspects can be found throughout in this groovy space.

Industry observers note that in the primary bedroom, Troy Rivington of Rivington Marx Interiors cocooned the room in a dark floral wallpaper and accessorized with other moody botanicals throughout. He was inspired by the romance of 1940s Cairo, dressing the room up like it belonged to a well-traveled collector.

As the first ever dedicated home gym at the Kips Bay Show House, Peter Hoffman of Platinum Gym Design chose a refined, luxurious setup. He named the room Tanren after the Japanese art of hammering and refining metal, and used walnut in both the equipment and the ceiling slats, stainless steel frames, and brown leather accents to complete the exercise space.

In this bespoke bathroom, Russ Peters and Bill Cates of Peters Cates Design lined the wall behind the Studio McGee x Kohler bathtub with a rich merlot tile by RIAD Tile. It’s a beautiful statement and a fabulous way to bring more texture and dimension to the room.

Recent findings suggest that in this tucked away library space, filled with collected finds, designers Christina Garcia Lysaught and Grayson Knight of Layered Dimensions finished off this dark space with a stunning statement mirror. Around the perimeter are resin busts of wildlife, like owls and deer, bringing in a bejeweled touch to the room.

Sources indicate that the small but mighty kitchen, designed by Katie Stephenson of Stephenson Home, is crowned with a crackled-gold blooming wallpaper, bringing a warm balance to the rest of the room. It’s covered in birds, butterflies, and blossoms, and it wraps the cook space in a golden glow, reminding all who enter that this room should be as beautiful as it is functional.

The citron paint color wrapping the walls in Jen Bienvenu’s entrance hall is undoubtedly enchanting and serves as the perfect backdrop for her “After the Hunt” theme, but it’s the lampshades made from old silk saris that tie everything together for us. They provide such a magical warmth and really capture the essence of a collector’s treasure room.

Step through the citron entry and enter the round room, designed in collaboration by Helen Bergin Interiors and Lichten Architects. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You deserve better than itchy, scratchy sheets on your bed at night. Upgrading your bedding is more than a bedroom aesthetic choice; it’s an investment in your well-being. I know this firsthand—as both a design editor and an insomniac. I’ve tested over a dozen of the best luxury sheets on the market in my journey to fix my sleep routine. The right sheet set lets me drift off much more easily, and I’m here to help you find one of your own.

What sets “luxury” sheets apart from your run-of-the-mill bargain bedding? It's a combination of texture, quality, aesthetic, and price point. The set should feel good the moment it hits your skin. The fabric, too, should be durable and constructed to avoid pilling, tearing, or any of that less-than-best feel. As the name implies, luxury sheets often come with a higher price tag, so you'll want to make sure they're worth the extra money.

In a recent development, I have every sleep concern you could think of: I'm a hot sleeper, I snore, I toss and turn, and I have eczema, so I have to be picky about what fabric goes in my bed. Luckily, my fellow editors, testers, and I have spent over three years sleeping on every kind of sheet under the sun, from fluffy flannel to silky eucalyptus. And now we’re revealing the ones that totally upgraded our sleep routines. Scroll on to meet our MVBs (most valuable bedding).

Recent findings suggest that I first tested the Buffy Breeze sheets in my evaluation, and beyond the beautiful sheen that made the sheets look luxe, the cooling feeling of the eucalyptus fibers completely won me over. After months of trying other sheets, these were still my favorite.

I'm an incredibly hot sleeper, and I can't stand waking up to sticky sheets. These sheets from Buffy, made from moisture-wicking eucalyptus, gave me the most refreshing sleep I've had in my life. The first quality that impressed me about these sheets was how well they shifted with my constant tossing and turning. Even as they gathered underneath me, I was never uncomfortable. They're lightweight and breathable without the gauzy texture of other airy sheets. I genuinely looked forward to sinking into them at the end of the day.

I also tested Buffy's Cloud pillows under the pillowcases in this set and was impressed with how well they held their shape, even as I bunched them up under my neck. I was convinced I’d have horrible neck pain any time I slept on a pillow that wasn’t the butterfly shape I have for side sleepers. Imagine how shocked I was by how comfortable and long I slept.

Colorways: 25 | Sizes: Full, Queen, King, Cal King | Materials: Eucalyptus (lyocell).

Quince bedding is one of the best ways to get that luxury sheet feel on a tighter budget. Tester Jessica Cherner has tested their bamboo, linen, and percale varieties, but the bamboo sheets stood out for their silky feel. "These sheets are so great because they have a tiny bit of stretch to them, which makes them even softer," Cherner claims. "What makes them so soft is the fact that they're made from 100 percent viscose bamboo (the pulp), which is a bit more luxurious than rayon.".

Colorways: 15 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, Cal King | Materials: 100 percent viscose from organic bamboo.

Many die-hard fans of cotton bedding can’t imagine sleeping on anything else. The cool, crisp feeling of Hommey’s striped cotton bedding is what won over McKenzie. “These are my perfect all-purpose sheets,” McKenzie notes. “It’s not for your hottest days or your coldest nights, but for all of the days that fall in between. It’s a sturdy, well-woven 100 percent organic cotton, designed for year-round use and reliable comfort. It has a crisp feel that maintains its shape, and it rarely wrinkles, even after I’ve spent all night tossing and turning. I’m also a hot sleeper, and any thread count above 400 TC starts to get a bit stuffy for my taste. These fall at a perfect 300 TC, thick enough to insulate from cool air.”.

Colorways: 28 | Sizes: Twin/Twin XL, Full/Queen, King/Cal King | Materials: 100 percent organic cotton.

Recent findings suggest that despite being a hot sleeper, McKenzie still needed a solid set of winter sheets for the coldest nights. The whipstitching on Boll & Branch’s flannel set made for a festive refresh in the holiday season. “I've also tested Boll & Branch's cashmere sheets, and those were more lightweight than the flannel, but they have the same brushed, soft weave,” McKenzie notes. “It's as durable as my Saatva flannel sheets, but not as stiff. They look super chic, like hotel sheets. It takes a lot for me to willingly own light-colored sheets, but these are just gorgeous. My favorite detail is the holly-red whipstitching; I just wish it went all the way around the border of the set. I was sad to take these off my bed to test the others.”.

Colorways: 15 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King w/ King Cases, King w/ Std. Cases, California King, Split King | Materials: 100 percent organic cotton.

Piglet in Bed allows customers to choose between 100 percent linen and linen-blend sheets, in order to maximize personal comfort. Tester Maggie Haddad opted for the linen blend and was pleasantly surprised. “After sleeping on this bedding for more than two months, I can confidently say I don’t see myself going back to traditional cotton sheets anytime soon,” Haddad says. “I initially worried that linen might feel too coarse or scratchy for my liking, but the linen blend turned out to be the ideal balance of softness and subtle texture.”.

Colorways: 13 | Sizes: Twin, Full, Queen, King | Materials: 100 percent linen or 55 percent European linen and 45 percent long staple cotton.

Don’t be intimidated by cashmere’s delicate nature. Though the cleaning instructions are specific, these sheets are worth extra TLC. “Just saying ‘cashmere sheets’ has an air of luxury, and Boll and Branch's set lives up to the hype. From night one, these sheets draped over me like silk, but were more buttery soft and fuzzy than cold and smooth. As someone who sweats easily, the lightweight feel was welcome. I'd still reach for these sheets in the summer, or whenever I had a guest I wanted to impress.”.

Colorways: 4 | Sizes: Queen, King with King Cases, Cal King | Materials: 92 percent extra-long-staple organic Turkish cotton, 8 percent cashmere.

Recent findings suggest that when contributing writer Kelsey Mulvey put these Luxome sheets to the test, every little detail wowed her, even as a sheets snob. "Unless I'm able to set the thermostat to an arctic temperature, I run hot when I sleep, so I'm always looking for bed sheets with cooling properties," Mulvey says. Not only is the viscose from bamboo used here moisture-wicking and temperature-regulating, so I'm not waking up in a pool of sweat, but they're also ridiculously silky smooth.".

Colorways: 12 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, Cal King, Split King | Materials: 100 percent Bamboo viscose.

Senior Commerce Editor Marina Liao notes that Parachute's linen sheets feel soft right out of the packaging and regulate one's body temperature better than other linen sheets. She uses these year-round. "I love that the sheets don't shed much, and I trust the brand to deliver consistent quality because of its transparency in providing details like GSM," Liao says. "The name evokes many positive associations in my mind, and this would be a nice luxury set I'd gift to someone moving into their first apartment.".

Colorways: 8 | Sizes: Full, Queen, King, Cal King | Materials: 100 percent European flax.

According to recent reports, cherner would pay twice as much for these Lands' End sheets. "Here's why: I prioritize softness over all else, and these are definitely some of the softest sheets I've ever slept on," Cherner states. "They don't really have a hint of crispness, so if that's your thing, you may not love these. Plus, when I think about the other supremely soft sheets I have—most of which are more than double the price of these Lands' End ones—I feel like I'm getting a bargain.".

Colorways: 8 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, Cal King, Split King | Materials: 100 percent Premium Supima cotton.

Recent findings suggest that I originally tested these sheets because they were designed for my latest Purple mattress, not expecting much. After months of sleeping on them, they'll be my new favorite all-purpose sheets. They're soft and stay put, so making the bed in the morning is a breeze. And I could use them no matter the season—they strike that perfect balance of warming and cooling. It's flowy and always looks neat. Even though it's meant to optimize the comfort of a Purple mattress, I'm confident it would make any mattress brand feel softer.

Colorways: 6 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, Cal King, Split King | Materials: 63 percent rayon from bamboo viscose, 27 percent polyester, 10 percent spandex.

As someone with sensitive skin, finding sheets that are gentle on my skin is essential. I don't want something scratchy and itchy that'll cause my eczema to flare up, so please trust me when I say they're the softest sheets I've ever tested. It's made of 700 threads of long-staple Giza cotton, for durability and warmth. Giza cotton is a sought-after, typically expensive fabric, so it's quite the steal to get a set for under $200. I normally only sleep on silk pillowcases, but I make an exception for how smooth this fabric is.

Colorways: 8 | Sizes: Twin, Full, Queen, King, Cal King | Materials: 100 percent Giza sateen cotton.

According to recent reports, is there anything cooler than sheets so comfy, they're approved by NASA? Tester Rachel Elliot put the Slumber Cloud Performance Cotton sheets to the test. The sheets are made from a unique blend of cotton and viscose that received the Certified Space Technology quality mark. Translation? The same technology used to design specialized NASA spacesuits is used for these DTC bedsheets. It's engineered to strike that perfect balance between a cozy feel and temperature regulation. They'll cool you off when you're hot and warm you up when you're cold. "I tried these in peak New York City winter and actually did feel warmed up after about 30 minutes in bed," Elliot notes. "Now that it's warm outside, I do have to admit that these are very crisp and cooling!".

Colorways: Four | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, Cal King | Materials: 30 percent Outlast viscose, 70 percent cotton.

Tester Laura Tarafa first tried Frette sheets on an Italy vacation in 2021, and she had some of the best sleep of her life. There's a reason five-star properties like the Le Sirenuse, Four Seasons Hotel Milano, and The St. Regis hotels use Frette linens. "Though the sheets were cotton, it felt like I was sleeping on a silk cloud, and I didn't slide around on the bed," Tarafa claims. "I was genuinely excited to end the day of sightseeing in Italy in order to get back into bed and feel the comfort of the sheets again! In fact, I loved them so much that while I was still on my trip, I ordered a few items from Frette's Lux Percalle collection and their H by Frette range to my home in Texas.".

Colorways: Two | Sizes: Queen, King, Cal King | Materials: 100 percent long-staple cotton.

After years of using Brooklinen's durable best-selling sheets, Mulvey still swears by them, not just for herself, but for guests. There's a delicate balance between crisp and uncomfortable when it comes to percale bedding, and Brooklinen stays firmly on the right side. "Over the years, my percale sheets have remained crisp and cool to the touch, but never feel stiff or scratchy," Mulvey states. "In fact, I like this set so much that I bought a Twin version for the trundle bed in our guest room—you know, to make my friends and family feel like they’re in a hotel.".

Tester Katelyn Lunders chose this set as her first sateen sheets, and loved the breathable feeling of the organic bamboo fabric. The hypoallergenic sheets are made with non-toxic solvents, so it's a great choice for sensitive skin. "Ettitude's fabric is incredibly soft, like the softest sheets I think I've ever slept on personally," Lunders says. "I love how lightweight and cooling they are, and they don't wrinkle as easily as my cotton sets. The only con I have is that because the fabric is on the thinner side, it slightly demonstrates the outline of my beloved Coop pillows, as you can see in the photo, but regardless, they are my current go-to.".

Colorways: 10 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, and Cal King | Materials: 100 percent Bamboo Lyocell.

It has been revealed that the craze around Thuma's bedding convinced skeptic tester Kate McGregor to give linen sheets another try, and she found a set that she loves. The bedding was still cozy to bundle in, even during a heatwave. "These sheets were breathable, but I found that I was comfortable and kept warm enough with just a top sheet as the layer," McGregor claims. "I didn’t notice any staining or wet spots due to my nightly Aquaphor layer.".

Colorways: Three | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, and Cal King | Materials: 100 percent European Flax Linen.

Brooklinen topped our list of the best bedding stores, so it stands to reason that their signature silky sheets would be the best in affordable luxury. The sateen finish has a certain luster to it, and the tightly woven sheets are built to last. "They're silky to the touch without feeling too slippery, and I prefer them over linen sheets in summer since they're just as cooling without looking wrinkled all the time," Tester Samantha Jones says. "I've had them for a little over a year now and haven't noticed any pilling, loose threads, or snagging.".

Colorways: 23 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, and California King | Materials: Organic cotton sateen.

In a recent development, cherner has been sleeping on this Boll and Branch set for over two years. Despite their luxury feel, they require very little to maintain their quality because the last thing you need is extra fuss in your bedtime routine. "I could sit on ten different brands's sheet sets and still tell you which ones are Boll & Branch," Cherner states. "They're extremely soft and feel so luxurious. I will say: They're on the thicker side, so I don't really use them in the summer, even with air conditioning, because I definitely sleep hot. This is easily one of my favorite brands.".

Colorways: 20 | Sizes: Twin, Twin XL, Full, Queen, King, Cal King, Split King | Materials: Organic long-staple cotton.

Industry observers note that you'll not only find The Citizenry's stonewashed linen bedding in House Beautiful editor bedrooms, but you'll also find it in Blake Lively's. We can't blame her either—the luxe yet lived-in look of these sheets is such an elegant, airy choice. "These sheets are made in a family-run textile mill in Portugal, and you can feel the quality," Deputy Commerce Editor Heath Owens says. "They're my favorite linen sheets that I've tried! They feature a really lightweight weave, which keeps them breezy and airy instead of scratchy. ".

Colorways: 15 | Sizes: Full, Queen, King, Cal King | Materials: Stonewashed linen.

In a recent development, both Cherner and our Senior Commerce Manager, Mackenzie Dunn consider themselves Cozy Earth devotees. After Cherner's test, she found that she loved how gentle the fabric was on her hair and skin. “Temperature-regulating and buttery soft, these sheets work for both my husband (a hot sleeper) and me (a cold one)," Dunn says. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Harrigan men don’t do flashy. For a family sitting on a drugs fortune that stretches from north London to a sprawling estate in the Cotswolds, they dress like they’re popping out for a pint: good tailoring, wax jackets, country staples, and nothing with a logo you could spot from across the room.

Their watches are no exception. There’s nothing loud or iced ou—just good, solid classics chosen by men who know their stuff. And they really do: In the very first episode, it turns out that one of the family’s side hustles is trading stolen cars for watches. So, somewhere in the Cotswolds, a Harrigan is almost certainly arguing about reference numbers on r/Watches.

Look closer, though, and the watches say more than just “good taste.” Each matches the job the man does for the family, so that watch tells you exactly where he sits in the pecking order. From the boss (Pierce Brosnan) down to the man who’s doing his dirty work, here’s how they line up.

Recent findings suggest that pierce Brosnan plays Conrad, the family’s head honcho—the guy who runs the empire without getting mud on his brogues (most of the time, anyway). And when you're at the top, you don’t need a watch that does much. No stopwatch, no dive bezel, no second time zone (that’s what the staff are for). So, Conrad wears a dress watch, and a decorative one at that: a gold Omega Constellation, with a fluted bezel and pie-pan dial that are there, purely, to look good. Like Conrad, though, it’s tougher than it looks: the Globemaster was Omega’s first Master Chronometer, tested to fend off magnetic fields of 15,000 gauss.

Sources indicate that then there’s the in-joke: Brosnan wore an Omega Seamaster during his time as 007, so seeing him return to his roots is a little Easter egg for anyone who’s paying attention. The sporty diver has been swapped with something more expensive but less practical—would you expect anything less for a retired Bond?

According to recent reports, kevin is the heir—the son, played by Paddy Considine, who’s waiting for that top job with one eye firmly on his dad’s will. So, fittingly, his watch feels a little eager. It’s a Breitling Premier B01 (the flash of yellow under the strap gives it away). A strong watch, for sure, it’s just the kind you buy when you want to look like the boss before you’ve secured the promotion. And it tracks: When Willy Breitling designed the OG Premier in the 1940s, it was the brand’s first watch made purely for style.

The real tell, though, is that it’s still working harder than his dad’s. Conrad’s gold Omega just tells the time, because Conrad hasn’t had much else to do in years. Kevin’s chronograph comes with pushers, sub-dials, and a stopwatch, plus around 70 hours of power reserve. The watch of a man who’s close to the throne, but not quite there yet.

It has been revealed that paul (Emmett J. Scanlan) is the Harrigans’ head of security and Conrad’s right-hand man—the one who’s always just a step away. And when the family’s estate comes under attack in Season 2, he, of course, is the one holding the fort. So, as you’d expect, there’s no gold here. Paul, instead, gets a tool watch.

Recent findings suggest that but it’s not just any old tool watch, it’s a serious tool watch: IWC’s Pilot’s Chronograph. From a long line of sturdy watches built for military pilots who needed to tell the time in an instant, it has a large steel case, big clear numerals, and it’s tough enough to survive being bashed around a little (which, in Paul’s line of work, is a regular occurrence). This one’s a vintage mechaquartz version which is a bit of a hybrid: a quartz movement keeps the time on track while the chronograph is mechanical. Part brains, part brawn. Sounds like the perfect head of security to us.
