💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that how do you turn a straightforward ranch-style home into something exciting and unexpected yet timeless?
  • Recent findings suggest that located in an old, established neighborhood on a lake in Winter Park, Florida, the home was surrounded by mature live oaks and beautiful landscaping.
  • According to recent reports, alongside Skolfield Homes, Farmer kept the architectural style generally the same, with the most impactful changes being a complete overhaul of the galley kitchen and a relocation of the staircase from the side of the house to the middle, putting it in its deserved place as a focal point of the living room.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that how do you turn a straightforward ranch-style home into something exciting and unexpected yet timeless? When a young family of four asked designer James Farmer to do just that for their central Florida abode, he opted for a gut renovation, using his homegrown knowledge of Southern style, years of interior expertise, and pointed enthusiasm to renovate ranches to create a highly functional and striking escape for his clients.

Recent findings suggest that located in an old, established neighborhood on a lake in Winter Park, Florida, the home was surrounded by mature live oaks and beautiful landscaping. “I would describe the area as old-school Florida with a touch of Mayberry,” says Farmer, referencing the fictional town from The Andy Griffith Show. The home itself was humble and honest—“no hiding its hand at the poker table,” says Farmer.

According to recent reports, alongside Skolfield Homes, Farmer kept the architectural style generally the same, with the most impactful changes being a complete overhaul of the galley kitchen and a relocation of the staircase from the side of the house to the middle, putting it in its deserved place as a focal point of the living room. The new kitchen is what he calls a “glorified galley,” with a sunny breakfast room off to the side that used to be a screened-in porch. He then reinforced the home as a "front door house," ensuring the formal entry space would actually be used rather than passed through by adding a bar perfect for fancy cocktail parties or a casual post-work martini.

For the actual interior, the designer layered various textures and bold patterns, combining them with hallmarks of grand Floridian style, like floral wallpapers, gold details, intricate trim, palm motifs, pecky cypress wallcoverings, and a coastal color palette. The line between indoor and outdoor living is further blurred with trellis details and a selection of timeworn brick and wood flooring. "We really leaned into this in a new way with this project because of its location," he says. "True, classic Florida can be so fun but also timeless, and that was our goal with this project.".

Farmer encouraged his clients to splurge only on materials and pieces that'll truly stand the test of time, opting for classic finishes and prints that will age with the young family—an approach he details intimately in his newest book, Home Again: A Return to Gracious Interiors. Ultimately, the decadent interior paired with the modern structural changes naturally created what ended up being Farmer's motto for the home: "Traditional with a twist!".

FAST FACTSDesigner: James Farmer of James Farmer DesignsLocation: Winter Park, FloridaThe Space: A ranch-style home with 4 bedrooms and 3.5 bathrooms.

Fabulous cocktail parties start in this formal space before migrating to other parts of the house. With no TV in the space, all eyes are drawn to the bar set behind a custom set of accent chairs by Thibaut, which is where Farmer's clients shake up (not stir) "the best martinis in Florida.".

Recent findings suggest that A color palette of peach, robin's egg blue, and butterscotch is celebrated in this room, the designer explains. By painting the ceiling in a blue tone—a trick commonly seen on Southern porches—he gave the room a subtle indoor-outdoor touch commonly seen on Southern porches.

Borrowed light from the kitchen and stairwell shines on the rich velvets and great patterns in this family room. “The color combo of terracotta and emerald with creamy white millwork creates a handsome and elegant palette,” Farmer adds.

It has been revealed that once a screened-in porch, Farmer kept the alfresco feel by covering the walls and ceiling with trelliage panels and outfitting the room with timeless white wicker furniture by Memoire Design (once known as Mainly Baskets Home). Vintage elephant garden stools now stand as whimsical side tables.

“We kept the original corner cabinets and wainscoting but gave it a bit of glam with a custom Gracie Studio wallpaper and lacquered ceiling,” Farmer says of the dining room, which kept its original footprint. The console tables are painted in a lemony yellow hue to match the window treatments and the room's other cheerful elements.

Industry observers note that farmer broke up this completely new, double galley kitchen into sections to make hosting a breeze. On one side of the counter is the seating and hangout zone, while the other side plays host to a functional working kitchen, outfitted with a Wolf range and Sub-Zero fridge. Think of it like traditional with a twist; "These clients are fabulous entertainers, and the island can also make a great buffet for parties," he indicates. "We like to think that The Golden Girls would thrive in this kitchen… Mid-century meets Maw-Maw!".

It has been revealed that old Chicago brick and palm motifs in the wallpaper make this breakfast hub feel more like a terrace than an interior enclave. Farmer created this room as part of the kitchen expansion—its bay window only enhances the porch-like vibe he wanted. "Sometimes geometry is your best friend," Farmer says, noting that the rug, table, and even shape of the room are octagonal. "You might not notice it, but it makes a moment.".

In a recent development, “We were able to move the staircase in this house, which allowed for a more efficient floor initiative for this young family,” he explains. “When you are under a major renovation, you can think outside of the box, or sometimes inside the box, just as easily.” Now the stairwell can live as a beautiful moment all its own at the center of the home, rather than pushed to the side.

Sources indicate that the daughter was sleeping in a crib when Farmer first started working on his clients' house, so he wanted to design a room that could grow with her (by the time the project wrapped, she was in her significant girl bed). The pink trellis wallpaper by Schumacher perfectly rides the line between feminine and elevated.

Touches of bamboo, palm, and pecky cypress introduce that old Florida feel, reminiscent of family vacations to the family's favorite spots in the Sunshine State, without being too on the nose.

“An interior design trick that is so old-school, but still so fun, is using a drapery fabric for wall covering and vice versa,” Farmer explains. “We were able to bring that from the primary bedroom to the primary bathroom.”.

In a recent development, james Farmer is a Southern author, interior designer, and speaker known for his ability to create beautifully familiar and welcoming homes. To James, a home engages all of the senses—the pleasantries of colors and materials, the feel of the doorknob warmed by the sun, the smell of fresh laundry, the sound of the closing door, and the taste of supper on the table. Through his design firm, James works with clients to truly create a home.

Recent findings suggest that projects by James Farmer Designs can be found from the countryside of Connecticut to James's home state of Georgia. Though his work can be found throughout the country, James proudly has built his business in his hometown of Perry, Georgia.

Designers Say "Cook's Tables" Are About to Replace Kitchen Islands in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For years, oversized kitchen islands have been the be-all and end-all, but lately, designers and homeowners are gravitating toward something a bit smaller: a cook’s table.
  • Unlike built-in islands that can sometimes dominate a kitchen and cover most of the available floor space, cook’s tables bring a lot of flexibility to the room.
  • The other benefit is the big charm factor they add.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pictured Above: A kitchen designed by Amy Sklar.

For years, oversized kitchen islands have been the be-all and end-all, but lately, designers and homeowners are gravitating toward something a bit smaller: a cook’s table.

Unlike built-in islands that can sometimes dominate a kitchen and cover most of the available floor space, cook’s tables bring a lot of flexibility to the room. Because they’re freestanding, you can move them around depending on your needs (especially if they’re on wheels), whether that’s for prepping meals, hanging out with your morning coffee, or helping kids with homework after school. They also tend to be narrower, making them the perfect solution for small kitchens.

The other benefit is the big charm factor they add. They’re often wooden, with traditional-looking design elements, like turned legs and curvy silhouettes. Cooks tables can also frequently be found in vintage and antique stores, so they’re a great way to work a bit of charm and patina into an otherwise utilitarian space.

As kitchens move away from ultra-sleek and minimal, pieces with warmth and character are becoming more and more popular, and a cook’s table is the perfect example of that. If you’re considering adding one to your own home, learn what to look for—and how to style it—below.

According to recent reports, one of the biggest reasons cook’s tables are trending right now is that they soften the overall look and feel of a kitchen. “A traditional island can dominate a kitchen,” states designer Amy Sklar. Because cook’s tables don’t have a bulky built-in base, they feel visually lighter and less imposing, especially in kitchens where space is limited.

Designers also point to the emotional shift happening in homes post-pandemic. “The pandemic reshaped the way we live at home, placing greater value on spaces designed for connection and togetherness,” indicates designer Becky Ducsik of The Phinery. “Nowhere is this more apparent than in the kitchen, where homeowners are reimagining how they gather and entertain.”.

According to recent reports, unlike traditional islands that are packed with appliances and storage, cook’s tables create a more communal focal point centered around gathering and spending time together. That relaxed atmosphere is part of what makes them feel so appealing. Designer Cynthia Lananh notes that cook’s tables strike a balance between practicality and personality, functioning as prep space, dining space, and entertaining hub all at once. “I love a kitchen island that looks like a piece of furniture,” she says, adding that the look feels more casual, approachable, and timeless than a standard built-in island.

It has been revealed that while cook’s tables can absolutely make a statement in a large kitchen, designers say they’re especially effective in kitchens with tighter footprints or galley-style layouts. Because they take up less visual and physical space than a traditional island, they can help smaller kitchens feel more open and airy.

That stated, larger kitchens can benefit from them too, just in a different way. “With the right vintage find or custom-crafted piece, it can anchor the room and become a striking centerpiece that adds both function and timeless appeal,” indicates Ducsik.

In a recent development, she recommends using cook’s tables as the focal point in kitchens where storage and appliances can be concentrated along the perimeter. Since seating typically wraps around all sides, she suggests leaving at least four to five feet of clearance around the table to maintain a comfortable flow.

For homeowners who want the look but don’t have space for a freestanding table in the center of the room, Ducsik also suggests integrating one as a peninsula extension at the end of cabinetry for a similar communal feel.

Unlike built-in islands, cook’s tables offer a level of flexibility that’s hard to beat. Since they’re freestanding, they can be moved or adapted more easily over time—a feature designers say is especially useful for entertaining.

Industry observers note that sklar points out that cook’s tables can create a flexible landing zone within a kitchen and are ideal for holidays or large gatherings when extra room is needed. “This is perfect for holidays and large gatherings where you need even more space,” Lananh states. She recommends adding casters if the table will double as both a prep and dining space, making it easier to move around as needed.

Scale is one of the most important things to get right: The table should feel proportional to the room while still leaving enough space to comfortably move around it. Height matters, too. Sklar notes that many vintage tables sit lower than standard counter height, so homeowners may need to modify them slightly with casters or leg extenders to make them more functional for prep work.

According to recent reports, as for materials, wood remains the go-to choice for warmth and character. “Durable woods (like oak, maple, or walnut) are popular for their warmth, strength, and character,” states Lananh. “Reclaimed wood adds rustic charm, whereas metal or butcher block tops offer a more durable, industrial aesthetic.”.

Ducsik echoes those sentiments and suggests echoing the table’s wood tones throughout the kitchen with details like open shelving, cutting boards, or serving pieces to create a cohesive look.

Recent findings suggest that lastly, focus on shape. Softer corners and curves can make the space feel more intimate, while rectangular tables can maximize seating and prep space. Ultimately, the goal is for the piece to feel like furniture, not cabinetry. And that’s exactly what makes cook’s tables so appealing in the first place.

In Glen Ridge, Newly introduced Jersey, a red-brick Georgian Colonial has a remarkable backstory. When a family of three bought the sprawling home in 2021, its history and architectural pedigree were part of the appeal, and they wanted to honor both while making the house feel like their own.

For designer Andrew Suvalsky, that meant striking the right aesthetic balance. “The biggest challenge was finding the sweet spot of grandeur and formality that is inherent to the house and its history, while making design choices that were suited to a more casual lifestyle,” he states.

Over a three-year renovation period, Suvalsky kept priceless details—like the original crown molding, gold architectural details, and the home’s many chandeliers—while giving the rest of the space a much-needed decor upgrade. “I’ve done traditional interiors, but this house is the most elaborate I’ve worked on, and the design had to meet the house on its level,” he notes.

The renovation touched nearly every room, from the billiards lounge to a fully remade kitchen. He also layered in luxe touches throughout: In the dining room, upholstered Fortuny panels bring a timeless elegance, while the bar’s walnut paneling and ornate cornucopia garland frame the fireplace.

Recent findings suggest that as Suvalsky spent more time in the house, its grand scale began to feel more intimate. “It helped me understand how building a house this size made sense for a family 120 years ago and how it can translate to a family’s life today,” the designer states. He sees the resulting space as meaningfully in dialogue with its deep history while looking ahead to the family’s future. “It’s nice to know that good architecture can truly stand the test of time.”.

#7573. Is This a ‘Gut Feeling’ About My Relationship... or Just My Anxiety?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (894 w)

Is This a ‘Gut Feeling’ About My Relationship... or Just My Anxiety?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (894 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • We’re often told that we should trust our gut in relationships—that when something is wrong, we’ll get a distinct feeling in our bodies.
  • In a recent development, I’ve had anxiety for as long as I can remember.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

We’re often told that we should trust our gut in relationships—that when something is wrong, we’ll get a distinct feeling in our bodies. But what if that feeling isn’t distinct at all? What if these feelings of dread and alarm are constant? What if you can’t really trust your gut?

In a recent development, I’ve had anxiety for as long as I can remember. And when I get into relationships, I feel the symptoms tenfold. I create worst-case scenarios in my head, over-analyze every little reaction, and go into a panic when a partner has the slightest shift in attitude. A lot of this anxiety has to do with my past (surprise, surprise). I was in an emotionally abusive relationship, riddled with infidelity and manipulation, for six years. And although it’s been years since my breakup and I’ve moved on to an entirely upcoming relationship that feels healthy and fulfilling, I don’t think my body and brain have quite gotten the memo.

According to recent reports, “A person who has experienced neglect, abandonment, unpredictability or inconsistencies in past relationships may be unknowingly conditioned to scan for threat, even in a healthy, stable relationship,” Jessica N. Gordon, LCSW tells Cosmopolitan.

So if you come equipped with intense relational trauma, how do you know the difference between when something is actually wrong in your relationship—and when it’s just your anxiety acting up again?

When every little thing feels like the end of the world, it becomes hard to discern when there’s a real concern in your relationship. This is typically what Relationship Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (ROCD) looks like.

Industry observers note that "Anxiety driven by ROCD tends to feel very intense and urgent,” Cameron Murphey, LMFT says. “It feels like you have to address it right now.” He explains that people with ROCD typically feel like they’re unable to focus on anything else until they've addressed what's making them feel anxious.

But the problem is what’s making them anxious isn’t exactly rooted in something concrete. People with ROCD constantly ruminate on thoughts like “How do I know I’m truly in love?,” “There have been no signs, but I think they’re cheating on me,” or “Is my partner doing enough?” There might not even be a specific action that triggers these thoughts.

Sources indicate that “An [ROCD] thought tends to jump from topic to topic... and feels spontaneous rather than a consistent subtle thought,” Gordon notes. A true concern in the relationship, on the other hand, is tied to real, observable behavior that highlights up in a pattern: “every time we talk about my feelings, he picks up his phone and I feel ignored.”.

But what if your gut is just screaming at you that something is wrong?

Recent findings suggest that “I think we sometimes give our gut feelings a lot of authority without stopping to consider what's informing them,” Sonni Williams, LPC says. “Our intuition can be shaped by our experiences, values, and even the things we're afraid of repeating.”.

She adds that we sometimes tend to oversimplify intuition as calm and anxiety as panic. The problem with this is that both of these things can feel convincing, and neither feeling alone tells us whether something is true.

Rather than torturing yourself with these thoughts as they come, Williams says it’s more effective and helpful to look at what happens afterward.

“Can you reflect on the concern and decide whether something needs attention?” she indicates to ask yourself. “Or are you repeatedly analyzing conversations and feelings, trying to find certainty?”.

Recent findings suggest that now this doesn’t mean you need an immediate answer in order to take your feelings seriously. Williams explains that when it comes to concerns involving abuse, coercion, or controlling behaviors, these things deserve attention regardless of whether anxiety or ROCD are present.

It has been revealed that it’s absolutely a good thing to reflect on your relationship and assess if it’s working for you. But Williams explains that what’s most vital is knowing the difference between evaluating your relationship and feeling like you have to constantly prove that it’s right or perfect.

And you may not be able to trust your gut, specifically, but that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t trust yourself—you just have to learn what that looks like in the context of your anxiety.

Recent findings suggest that "Self-trust is not about believing that you'll always make the right choice,” Murphey notes. “It's about trusting that you can handle whatever happens, good or bad.”.

He explains that we tend to feel fear in our stomachs, so it’s easy to confuse those very physical feelings with something grander like intuition. And guess what? That’s totally fine—so long as you don’t use those feelings to solely dictate your actions in your relationship. If you get those feelings, think about why or where they’re coming from.

You’re going to have second thoughts about your partner from time-to-time (or if you’re me, every three business days). Seeing a therapist for lingering, uncontrollable thoughts can help you work through whatever anxieties you may have. Otherwise, there are going to be times where you just inevitably question your relationship.

Gordon indicates, “The goal is to feel less controlled by doubt, not to never have it.”.

The turkey may be the main event of Thanksgiving dinner, but it can be a snack, too! Whether you're hosting Thanksgiving for your community or celebrating with family, this fun appetizer is the perfect way to get everyone excited for the big turkey dinner with another smaller turkey! This cheese ball is not only the most eye-catching appetizer you can add to your holiday menu, but it’s surprisingly easy to create.

Industry observers note that what People Are Saying:“I made this for Friendsgiving. It was delicious and I got several comments on how great it tasted.” - kellykcox34580.

In a food processor, pulse the cream cheese, goat cheese, butter, and garlic powder until the mixture is smooth. Add parsley, chives, and thyme and pulse until well combined. Then season with salt and black pepper.

Industry observers note that transfer the cream cheese mixture to a piece of plastic wrap and gather up the wrap to form a ball. Then transfer the mixture into a large bowl and refrigerate until it’s firm, which should take at least three hours and up to one day.

In a clean food processor, pulse 3/4 cup pecan halves until they are finely chopped.

Transfer the pecans to a plate.

Roll the cheese ball in nuts and arrange it all on a platter.

Sources indicate that start by cutting a large triangle from a red bell pepper—this will be the face. Next, cut a smaller triangle from a yellow bell pepper for the beak. For the eyes, slice two small rounds from a small carrot. Take a larger carrot and slice it into diagonal ovals to make the feet, then carve little triangles at one end to look like toes. Finally, thinly slice the rest of the carrots into matchsticks for the tail.

In a recent development, grab some toothpicks and stick the carrot eyes onto the red triangle face. Then, use another toothpick to add the yellow beak to the face—just make sure all the toothpicks point toward the back so you can attach everything to the cheese ball later. Now, press the face onto the front of the cheese ball, and slide the carrot feet into the base.

Sources indicate that insert matchstick carrots, pretzel sticks, and mini pretzels into the back of the ball to create the tail. Using the remaining 1/2 cup pecan halves, create wings by overlapping them along each side of the ball. Serve with crackers alongside!

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

According to recent reports, store leftover cheese ball in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. If possible, remove the pretzels and vegetable decorations before storing, as they can soften over time.

Sources indicate that as rain poured down on Manhattan Thursday night, so did the tributes to Steven Spielberg. The veteran director was honored at this year’s MoMA Film Benefit, presented by Chanel, with homages from fellow icons of cinema and collaborators including Martin Scorsese, Tom Cruise, Emily Blunt, and Ariana DeBose. To top off the night, Spielberg (and the crowd) was treated to a surprise acoustic performance by Bruce Springsteen.

Honoring Spielberg’s contributions to film feels like a no-brainer, given the dozens of masterpieces he has delivered in his decades-long career, spanning Jaws, E.T., the Indiana Jones franchise, Schindler’s List, Jurassic Park, Saving Private Ryan, and many more, all the way up to Disclosure Day, which was just released this summer. Reflecting on his latest, Spielberg said in his speech, “It’s less about aliens and more about empathy. Empathy is the only real superpower that humanity possesses. It’s the only form of magic, I think, that exists in the world.”.

And while he accepted the honor solo, the director remarked he shares the recognition with the hundreds of people in his casts and crews, including those who work at craft services. He also took a moment to thank his wife.

“When you honor me, you are also honoring my wife, Kate Capshaw, because the stuff I put in each of my films is from the stuff of life, real life, that Kate and I have created with family, friends, and conversation, and being aware that there’s more to living than just what we do for a living,” he said. “The confidence she’s given me every day for the past 43 years, I would not be the same person, or the same filmmaker, without her central to my very human existence.”.

The program included opening remarks from Cruise, who starred in Minority Report and War of the Worlds, followed by a speech from Scorsese, who reflected on his decades of friendship with Spielberg. “Listen, we’ve known each other since 1972—how did we get to be in our eighties? What happened?” he joked. DeBose, who starred in Spielberg’s West Side Story remake and won an Oscar, performed “Somewhere” from the legendary musical.

According to recent reports, blunt, who starred in Disclosure Day, revealed that the back of Spielberg’s director’s chair is labeled with “Dad.” “‘Dad’ still has this childlike enthusiasm, this spontaneity,” she stated. And when he’s “happy with a take, you’ll see him, he’ll just come running out of the tent with his fists in the air, and he’s cheering, and it’s like the best damn moment of your career,” she added. Spielberg later returned the praise, saying Blunt “could play any role—including James Bond.”.

According to recent reports, steve Martin and Martin Short alternated zippy one-liners while introducing the guest of honor (they even joked about how many awards they shared between the three of them). And Stephen Colbert helped introduce the grand finale, Bruce Springsteen, who sang “Dancing in the Dark” on his guitar. Before jumping into song, The Boss took a moment to say a few words about Spielberg too, recalling the summer when Jaws first came out when he was living on the Jersey Shore. There used to be a tradition called night swimming, where people would swim in the ocean nude, often with someone they were interested in. But ever since Jaws, “Steven Spielberg fucked that up. He fucked it up good,” Springsteen said, to a room of laughter.

Recent findings suggest that other attendees included Drew Barrymore, Cate Blanchett, Robert De Niro, Jeff Goldblum, Riley Keough, John Krasinski, Donna Langley, Spike Lee, Lorne Michaels, Michelle Pfeiffer, Zoe Saldaña, Francesca Scorsese, Christopher Walken, and Michelle Williams. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that heat a large skillet with oil and season the chicken with salt.
  • Then reduce the heat and add the onion, bell peppers, garlic, piment d’Espelette, and salt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rich tomatoes, stewed onions and peppers, and tender bone-in chicken make this Spanish- and French-inspired poulet Basquaise recipe extremely flavorful while still being surprisingly easy to make. Savory and rustic, it’s a stew that’s ideal for making ahead and enjoying all week long. The key ingredient? Piment d’Espelette—the regional spice known for its peppery, smoky essence. If you’re looking to master a classic dish or simply want a reliable, cozy weeknight dinner, then this recipe won’t let you down.

Industry observers note that heat a large skillet with oil and season the chicken with salt. Working in batches, add the chicken pieces and sear until the skin is golden in color, which should take 5 to 7 minutes. Remove the chicken to a heatproof plate.

Then reduce the heat and add the onion, bell peppers, garlic, piment d’Espelette, and salt. You’ll want to stir this once in a while so it doesn’t stick, but also let the vegetables soften. This should take 8 to 10 minutes.

At this point, increase the heat again and add the wine. Scrape up any bits on the bottom and allow those peppers and onions to absorb the wine. The liquid should reduce.

Add the tomatoes and broth and bring to a simmer. Be careful of splattering sauce and adjust the heat as needed. Place the chicken back into the skillet, skin side up, and cook until the chicken is tender and nearly falling off the bone. The sauce should also be thicker and fragrant. This should take about 30 to 40 minutes.

It has been revealed that stir in the chorizo and cook until it’s warmed through. Top it off with thyme and serve!

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Let cool and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. It’s certainly a great meal-prep dish. Make this on a Sunday night for lunch Monday and Tuesday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that puerto Rico has long been one of my favorite island destinations for a little rest and relaxation. Time and again, I find myself drawn back to the charming towns dotted along its northern and northeastern coasts. This month, my travels brought me to Río Grande, a tranquil, picturesque municipality affectionately known as La Ciudad de El Yunque (The City of El Yunque).

Industry observers note that just a 30-minute drive from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport, Río Grande offers a calmer setting than the bustling streets of San Juan, while still keeping the capital city’s attractions within easy reach. Beloved for its lush landscapes, breathtaking scenery, and abundant flora and fauna, the area is also home to a significant portion of El Yunque National Forest, which, fun fact, is the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. National Forest System.

Whether you prefer lounging poolside with a piña colada, venturing into the rainforest for a scenic hike, or heading west to meander through the vibrant streets of Old San Juan, I’ve found that Río Grande makes for an idyllic home base to experience the best of what the island has to offer.

Ahead, discover my recommendations for where to stay, what to eat, and what to explore in this enchanting corner of Puerto Rico.

Taking a nature walk or scenic hike through El Yunque National Forest is a must when visiting Río Grande. Whether you book a guided tour or venture out on your own with a rental car, there are trails suited to every experience level. Along the way, you’ll be stunned by the sheer variety of plants and wildlife you encounter. On my trip, I finally put a face to the symphony of chirps I’d been hearing throughout my stay: the Puerto Rican spindalis, a small, yellow-bellied bird native to the island.

It has been revealed that the forest is also home to a seemingly endless variety of tropical trees, mushrooms, orchids, and ferns. Climb the spiral staircase of the Yokahú Observation Tower for panoramic views of the lush green canopy and surrounding mountain peaks, and be sure to pack water shoes if you fancy a refreshing dip in one of the forest’s rivers or natural waterfall pools.

Whether you’re an avid golfer or just getting into the sport, Río Grande has several world-class courses worth exploring. Among them is Bahía Beach Golf Club, an 18-hole, par-72 course designed by renowned golf course architect Robert Trent Jones Jr. in 2008. Stretching 6,890 yards through lush tropical landscapes, the course features 15 holes bordering water, with beautiful rainforest views along the way. You’ll wind around scenic lakes before reaching the Atlantic coastline for the final few holes, making for an unforgettable morning or afternoon on the green.

Sources indicate that set sail from the nearby town of Fajardo for a morning, afternoon, or all-day affair spent exploring nearby islands with seemingly untouched beaches. Popular destinations include Culebra and Icacos Island, where you can lounge on the boat, soak up the sun, swim in crystal-clear waters, or snorkel among vibrant coral reefs teeming with colorful fish.

Sources indicate that perla, located at Four Seasons, opened this November under the direction of executive chef Victor Rosado and became one of my favorite dining spots during my visit. Taking its name from the Spanish word for “pearl,” the elegant restaurant offers a tempting selection of small bites, from pillowy Parker House rolls served with smoked butter to spicy salmon mousse, alongside standout seafood dishes like hamachi and Chilean sea bass.

The thoughtfully designed interior boasts natural wood accents and bold contemporary artwork, with sweeping ocean views to admire between courses. As for what to order, don’t miss the oyster brûlée with yuzu kosho hollandaise and crispy Ibérico ham, the prime New York strip steak served with Hasselback potatoes, or the tender octopus accompanied by creamy potato causa.

For lunch, head to Don Pepe, a longtime local favorite where the atmosphere is casual and the focus is on authentic Puerto Rican cooking made with quality ingredients and bold flavors. The menu spans traditional favorites like beef piononos and mofongo served with your choice of protein and sauce, alongside heartier, mouthwatering dishes like succulent grilled pork loin, the restaurant’s signature burger, and lobster risotto. The extensive cocktail menu also offers a tempting selection of tropical concoctions made with locally produced Don Q rum.

According to recent reports, another recent addition to the dining options at the Four Seasons Resort is Ocean Terrace, a picturesque open-air restaurant set along the shoreline. Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, the restaurant has a varied menu with something to satisfy every craving.

It has been revealed that mornings begin with a generous breakfast buffet, and if you have a sweet tooth like me, the coquito French toast on the à la carte menu is a must-try. For lunch, you’ll find everything from truffle honey stracciatella served with ciabatta to salads, pizzas, and sandwiches. Come dinnertime, I’d recommend exploring the selection of freshly made pastas, especially the creamy carbonara with pancetta—a dish I’m still dreaming about.

Zara Embroidered Eyelet Midi Dress.

Anine Bing Lili Tote Raphia Bag.

When you’re in the mood for a glamorous, atmospheric lounge to sip cocktails, head to Palm Court. The sleek, modern interior features plush seating that invites you to settle in and unwind, while a grand, square-shaped white marble bar serves as the room’s centerpiece. Beyond the elegant interior, an outdoor terrace offers additional seating for those who prefer to dine or enjoy a drink in the warm ocean breeze.

Industry observers note that located at the Bahía Beach Club, Sugar Beach Bar is a laid-back, open-air spot serving flavorful cocktails and delicious shareable bites. Sip on a tasty tropical cocktail made with local rum or tequila while soaking up stunning views of the ocean waves and Sugar Beach Pool.

Situated right by the Bahía Beach driving range, El Cocoteros Grill is a casual spot to unwind with a local beer. Open for breakfast and lunch, the restaurant offers a relaxed atmosphere, modern furnishings, and scenic rainforest views. And if you’re out on the golf course, you can even have drinks delivered straight to your golf cart.

Vestirsi Vivi Woven Shoulder Crossbody.

Saint Laurent Tribute Leather Slides.

Recent findings suggest that you can always count on a five-star stay at a Four Seasons, and the recently opened Four Seasons Resort and Residences Puerto Rico, nestled within the picturesque Bahía Beach community, is no exception. Set across 483 acres of spectacular tropical landscape, the resort boasts 104 guest rooms, 35 luxurious suites, and an impressive collection of private residences. The property has rightfully earned a coveted Michelin Key in recognition of its exceptional grounds, hospitality, and dining.

It has been revealed that the accommodations are everything you’d expect from the hotel organization, with luxe, modern furnishings, 24-hour in-room dining, and an attentive concierge team that can arrange everything from dinner reservations to rainforest excursions. The location also doubles as a private nature reserve, with conservation efforts that include rain gardens and sea turtle nesting protection. Guests can explore the surrounding wildlife and tropical flora through guided nature experiences, all without leaving the vicinity. And if you find yourself wishing you could stay a little longer, the dreamy private residences offer a more permanent escape to paradise.

As for how to spend your days, take your pick among lounging along the resort’s two miles of pristine beachfront, cooling off in one of the two swimming pools, or heading out to explore the island.

In a recent development, A golf lover’s dream, Bahía Beach Resort & Golf Club offers a more residential take on the traditional resort experience. Visitors can enjoy a private getaway in one of the community’s luxurious villas and residences, many of which are available for short-term rentals. Among them is Paradise View Villa, an incredible two-bedroom, three-bathroom property that comes with a six-passenger golf cart for getting around the grounds. Guests also have access to an array of resort amenities, including the golf club, tennis facilities, a fitness center, and the Lakehouse, where a variety of water sports await.

Ideal for families, larger groups, or those planning a special celebration, Wyndham Grand Rio Mar has 400 guest rooms, including 40 spacious suites with refined, colorful furnishings. With so much to see and do on the property, you could easily spend your entire getaway without venturing beyond the resort. Indulge in restorative treatments at El Yunque Spa, spend a lazy afternoon under the sun on the beach, or enjoy a round of golf at the scenic Rio Mar Country Club.

Veronica Beard Birke Merino Wool Tank Top.

Faithfull The Brand The Linen Pant.

Loeffler Randall Jovie Brown Jelly Flip Flop.

Color Wow Mini Extra Strength Dream Coat Anti-Frizz Treatment Spray.

According to recent reports, if your hair is prone to frizz, be sure to pack an anti-frizz treatment spray. My go-to is Color Wow’s Extra Strength formula, which works wonders in humid climates.

EltaMD UV Clear Broad-Spectrum SPF 46 Sunscreen.

SPF is a must when traveling to Puerto Rico, and EltaMD’s lightweight, dermatologist-recommended sunscreen absorbs quickly while helping soothe skin prone to acne and rosacea.

Summer Fridays Travel Sunlit Vanilla Fine Fragrance.

With its dreamy blend of warm caramel and sweet vanilla, Summer Fridays’ Sunlit Vanilla is the perfect fragrance to pack for a tropical escape.

  • Industry observers note that what kinds of changes are happening?
  • Here, nine unconventional ways to play with your bed pillow arrangements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A standard pillow setup—two king pillows against the headboard, with two standard pillows in the front, and a square accent pillow in the center—is a snooze. Designers are treating the bed as an opportunity to showcase a bit of flair. Not to mention awaken the entire bedroom.

Industry observers note that what kinds of changes are happening? Throw and accent pillows are now treated as if they are fashion accessories. We’re seeing everything from edgy studs to romantic ruffles in contrasting colors to graphic lines that hypnotize. In fact, mismatched pieces work great and can feel “intentional, collected, and completely joyful,” notes designer Betsy Wentz.

Here, nine unconventional ways to play with your bed pillow arrangements.

If the rest of your bedroom is neutral, designers are saying it’s OK to go more bold with your bed pillows. In the above space, it’s impossible not to notice the hypnotizing hue of Yves Klein blue pillows on a striped duvet cover.

“There’s something about that particular blue,” says designer Kate Anlyan, founder of Yasu Home. “It’s so vivid and almost electric, but it also has a depth to it. I love how it cuts through all the other tones without feeling disconnected from the rest of the room.” The hue works as a counterpoint to the wood paneling in the background and provides a balance to the visual weight of the black headboard.

Sources indicate that the interconnection between the contrasting stripes on the square pillows and the round velvet ball feels both fun and sophisticated, says designer Beth Diana Smith. The stripes feel especially striking, bringing a sense of energy and definition to the space, when set against the moody purple-brown Benjamin Moore's Cinnamon Slate wall color. To keep the rest of the bedding from competing, Smith tames the room with a muted light gray coverlet.

In a recent development, “Match up the headboard, throws, lamps and artwork with your throw pillows to balance out color throughout your room,” says designer Renée Gaddis. The encapsulated look creates instant cohesion. Starting with a bold hue, like a mustard yellow, will make your job easier because it has personality from the start.

Industry observers note that faux fur is a classic way to add rich texture, but you don’t need to reserve it for a château. Interior designer Mialani Collard uses a neutral linen palette and tactile embellishments that sandwich the fluff to make it less prominent, allowing the bed to work even in tropical climates like Florida.

In a recent development, when you want a home with casual living as the main objective, fill surfaces in a way that doesn't look too pristine or orderly. Interior designer Tyson Ness of Studio Ness mixed different patterns and colors for the bedroom pillows so there’s no “right way” to make the bed after it’s been used.

“The different combinations create a slightly different look each time, keeping the overall feeling light, airy, and totally casual,” Ness adds.

Choosing pillows that match the bedding is easy, but Cate Gutter, owner and principal designer of CWG Design, prefers to add a bit of je ne sais quoi when she styles the bed.

“This bedroom is tucked away in a mountain home here in North Carolina, and we wanted it to have a playful, nostalgic feel reminiscent of summer camp,” Gutter says. “We carried that inspiration into the pillow designs, giving them an almost handmade, craft-like quality that feels whimsical.”.

The oversized pillows are made in Imogen Heath's Arty Check, a cheerful yellow check finished with a fuzzy green fringe. In front of it, a smaller bolster is a playful take on a traditional shape, but the muted, multicolored stripe with a contrasting ruffled flange bolsters extra personality. The added texture breaks up the monotony of solid linens.

According to recent reports, “Studs are an unexpected detail on bed pillows because they’re so versatile,” claims Sean Carter, senior interior designer at Sapphire Pear. “They look just as great on a neutral fabric as they do with bold colors, prints, and patterns.” The metallic element adds a little edge without overpowering the overall design.

Wentz is no stranger when it comes to combining patterns and layering different scales in the same color family. Look for prints with their own personality that won’t compete with each other.

“The smaller confetti and stick stripe pillows give your eye a place to rest against that major graphic headboard, so they feel like friends, not strangers,” Wentz claims.

Pillows gone wild can still balance restraint. Creating serious contrast—in pattern direction—will step up your bedscaping game.

In a recent development, “The geometric patterns in the pillows complement the strong linear elements,” indicates interior designer Nicole Johnson. “The vertical wood slats draw the eye upward, while the horizontal lines of the bed and furnishings provide balance.”.

Linear patterns in the pillows at a smaller scale create a picture-in-picture effect that won’t overwhelm the overall design.

#7561. The Complicated Politics of Forgiving a Pop Star

The Complicated Politics of Forgiving a Pop Star

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s official: Slayyyter has graduated from being a gay guy music video night staple to a full-on Grammy nominee since dropping her first major-label album, WORST GIRL IN AMERICA.
  • The underdog has seemingly become a Main Pop Girl before our very eyes.
  • It has been revealed that but what happens when the pains of her past finally catch up to her ascent?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s official: Slayyyter has graduated from being a gay guy music video night staple to a full-on Grammy nominee since dropping her first major-label album, WORST GIRL IN AMERICA.

The underdog has seemingly become a Main Pop Girl before our very eyes. She drew a record-breaking 50,000 people at Lollapalooza and her first-ever headlining show at Madison Square Garden sold out in minutes. Her viral hit, “CRANK,” even landed a perfectly placed needle-drop in the equally awards-buzzy film Club Kid. These are only a fraction of the feats that prove her Best New Artist nod has been years in the making and, dare I say, rightfully earned.

It has been revealed that but what happens when the pains of her past finally catch up to her ascent? At the height of her breakout year, old social media posts using racial slurs resurfaced and introduced new fans to her regrettable history just as she was building momentum for the Grammys.

Though she had previously taken accountability for her behavior in 2020, she seemingly surrendered to the recent “Slayyyter Is Over Party” conversations fueling Stan Twitter with a post on her private account.

“This newfound attention is cool and all, but it’s unsettling about having people try to find things to ruin me with,” she reportedly wrote. “Why do you want to see me fail so bad?”.

Sources indicate that slayyyter isn’t the first pop star to have old social media behavior resurface as her career reaches new heights. Ethel Cain penned a four-page statement acknowledging her racist posts after the controversy surrounding them escalated, including the doxxing of her family and partner. When Camila Cabello’s use of the N-word resurfaced in 2021, she publicly apologized and took part in weekly racial healing sessions. While the circumstances aren’t identical, each situation raises questions about what accountability looks like when a pop star’s past follows them into a new chapter.

“Everyone has to be online to build their brand and promote their work in 2026, but a lot of times, the parasocial relationship that leads to monumental disappointment for some fans when they find out their fave isn't perfect is due to their being online,” comedian and podcast host Akilah Hughes, who called Slayyyter out for her recent response, tells Cosmopolitan.

Hughes only discovered the artist this past year after hearing her songs in several New Music Friday roundups. She admits that she “was definitely paying attention” to each drop and “was ready to be ‘early’ on” her music until those old posts popped up on her social feeds.

“I don’t think Slayyyter is necessarily a victim, though it’s definitely unfortunate that—as she’s put out this great album and is in the midst of a huge ascent—her own behavior is haunting her,” she explains.

Industry observers note that for Kiara Smith, a culture writer and podcast host who has followed Slayyyter since 2019, her posts brought a different kind of disappointment. At first, she was skeptical about the scandal’s reemergence.

“It seemed like someone just resurfaced the posts to start drama, rather than actually caring about what she remarked,” Smith tells Cosmopolitan.

Recent findings suggest that in the heat of the hate train, consumers allegedly started piling on fabricated screenshots that falsely depicted her as targeting Black recording artist Normani. Smith acknowledges that while she should be held accountable for the real posts, the fake ones serve no additional purpose.

Recent findings suggest that “What she remarked was terrible and inexcusable, but we have to be accurate when sharing things so as not to cause further harm to Black people for no reason,” Smith shares. “Black trauma is not a hot-button topic to debate. Tweets like that hurt real people and should be treated seriously.”.

Hughes echoes a similar sentiment. “For a lot of young people, being the perfection police is a way to gain clout online,” she says. “Having an encyclopedic knowledge of the times everyone has messed up is akin to power.”.

She continues, “Offline, in the real world, people are much more willing to give grace and additional chances. Because real life affords nuance, and the internet affords none.

“I think the internet is a very unforgiving place and has no place for nuance,” Smith adds. “If a person fucks up in real life, you can not fuck with them all you want. But in the end, I think everyone should want that person to be better and learn from their mistakes.”.

But is that grace extended equally? Can an artist—particularly a female artist—ever really overcome her past mistakes?

Slayyyter did her part years ago, yet she’s forced to revisit her past and educate herself as she reaches newly introduced levels of fame. Male counterparts like Chris Brown and Morgan Wallen have historically been awarded second (and third…and fourth) chances for other serious offenses, yet have continued to enjoy commercial success and industry support.

“We know that the internet and the world are way less forgiving to women. If you’re a woman, you have to do 10 times more to come back from a controversy,” Smith notes. “Lots of people have had controversies where they say a lot of nothing, but when this first came out years ago, Slayyyter seemed genuinely apologetic and even donated to many Black people and organizations afterwards. Not to say that excuses it, but we have to consider the effort she’s already made.”.

It has been revealed that two things can be true: while pop stars should be held accountable for such offenses, they should also be able to reflect and move forward. This isn’t to defend or endorse their actions, but to invite fans and artists to have more productive conversations—especially as this vicious cycle of scarlet letter-stamping continues to be normalized, particularly with female acts.

It has been revealed that accountability doesn’t guarantee forgiveness, nor should it. But that doesn’t mean any possibility of growth should be off the table, and Slayyyter has seemingly come to peace with that.

When describing her personal thesis behind WORST GIRL IN AMERICA to Cosmopolitan back in March, she nearly prophesied what her come-up would inevitably entail.

Recent findings suggest that “You can’t really escape where you’re from,” she stated. “You can change and grow into something better, but the things that happen to you when you’re young—you carry them with you for the rest of your life.”.

This Unexpected French Antique Is Suddenly Making a Comeback, and You’ve Probably Seen It Before

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The desire to preserve mementos from a wedding day transcends centuries and cultures.
  • It has been revealed that these ornate, shrine-like displays primarily showcased the bride's head crown and other keepsakes from the massive day, and the additional pieces inside symbolized the couple's dreams for their life together.
  • Here's a closer look at the history and allure of globes de mariée, plus tips for sourcing and styling these gorgeous antiques.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The desire to preserve mementos from a wedding day transcends centuries and cultures. Today's brides still hang onto their wedding dresses, dry their bouquets, and spend a large portion of their budgets on photography. But in 19th- and 20th-century France, the art of preserving wedding-day memories took the form of globes de mariée, also known as marriage globes.

It has been revealed that these ornate, shrine-like displays primarily showcased the bride's head crown and other keepsakes from the massive day, and the additional pieces inside symbolized the couple's dreams for their life together. The cloche protected these special items from dust back then and still today.

Here's a closer look at the history and allure of globes de mariée, plus tips for sourcing and styling these gorgeous antiques.

Chris Featherston is the senior vice president of product acquisition at Austin Auction Gallery, and he and his family have been dealing in French antiques for more than 30 years. In the last couple of years alone, they've sold more than 150 globes de Mariée for an average of $400 to $600 each.

According to recent reports, but this definitely wasn't always the case. Featherstone notes that the demand for these antiques has risen significantly in the past five years alone.

In a recent development, "In the early days of our business, most of what we sold came from house clearances in France," he recalls. "These globes were ubiquitous. At that time, we felt lucky to be able to sell them for $30 to $40 each.".

Industry observers note that anyone with a strong appreciation for historic relics can see the appeal of these antiques. For instance, Mick and Paige Whitcomb have been collecting globes de mariée for nearly a decade, and they currently own 15. Their interest in these types of treasures is reflected in their careers. Mick creates sculptural lighting from architectural and industrial salvage dating back to the 1800s through his business, Artifacts by Nomad. Paige is a tintype photographer who captures staged scenes featuring antiques from the 1800s (including her globes de mariée) using a 19th-century large-format studio camera.

Recent findings suggest that "While traveling in France for a wedding anniversary, we were first exposed to globes de mariée at the Marché aux Puces antique market in Paris," Mick says. "While we were initially caught by the beauty of the objects, after hearing their history and connection to French marriages, it felt like a beautiful way of commemorating our anniversary and trip to Europe.".

In a recent development, due to the highly custom nature of globes de marriée, each one is a unique find. However, Featherston notes that most contain a few similar components. For starters, the bride's headpiece often rests on a red cushion, and it typically highlights off delicate beeswax orange blossoms that symbolize purity and virginity.

Most also contain small mirrors, which carried different meanings depending on the shape. For example, diamond-shaped mirrors symbolize how many children the couple wished to have, and rectangular mirrors stood for the length of time the couple knew each other before their engagement.

Recent findings suggest that you'll also often find a wreath embellished with brass ornaments, usually flowers, birds and tree leaves. These symbolize love, a long-lasting marriage, and happiness.

"The globes de marriées integrate beautiful symbolism in every piece, and I find them fascinating," Paige says. "Each globe is so distinctive, and tells the story of the couple that created it. You can surmise the couple's hopes and dreams by minutiae tucked away behind the dome for safekeeping. I find very intimate details incorporated into the displays, such as a prayer card of a favorite saint, to photos of the bride and groom. I have even found hair and teeth, transforming the antique into a memento mori as well.".

Sources indicate that mick has noticed that sourcing these antiques is considerably more difficult in the United States than in Europe. But with a little patience and determination, it is possible.

"Because of the glass domes, I think fewer importers are brave enough to bring them over," he indicates. "Despite this, we have found the occasional gem in the wild." In the States, he's had the most luck sourcing them from design-forward antique dealers, online auction sites and even prop houses that have just wrapped up a period film project.

Since there is a constant demand for these pieces, Featherston tries to feature several in every sale at Austin Auction Gallery.

Globes de mariée can add a formal and traditional flair to any space, and they even mix well with more modern accents.

Sources indicate that "One of my favorite ways to showcase the globes de mariée is to mix them with a piece of contemporary art," Paige indicates. "I love to create a harmony between our collections of antiques and artwork from artists that are living and working today.".

Recent findings suggest that for example, Mick and Paige have styled two of their favorite globes de mariée with the piece "The Gardener" by working artist L.J. Eidolon. "I find collecting modern works that have a historic feeling to them helps create balance between the multiple centuries displayed together in one scene," Paige claims.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m always noticing something cool in someone else’s home and thinking, “Oh, I need that, too.” That happened last year when my family stayed with my in-laws. It was my first time seeing their newly renovated kitchen, and after a quick tour, one small detail caught my eye: the pop-up outlet in the kitchen island.

In a recent development, it was simple, practical, and exactly the kind of feature I wanted in my own kitchen. When we recently renovated our cook space, it went to the top of our wish list—and it has indeed been a game-changer with how we use the area.

Ahead, here’s why I love having a pop-up outlet, what to consider before installing one, and a few other kitchen gadgets that you might want to consider adding to your next upgrade.

Recent findings suggest that like the name suggests, a pop-up outlet is basically an electrical outlet that hides inside your countertop until you need it. Most models have a top you press or pull, and the outlet rises up so you can plug in your blender, mixer, or whatever else you're using. When you're done, you push it back down and it's out of sight.

Industry observers note that there are a few different versions, including ones that pop up manually and others that rise with the push of a button. Some, like the one we have, include USB ports or wireless charging built in. The outlet connects to power underneath the countertop, so it's something you'll want to blueprint for before your new counters go in.

Like pretty much any kitchen gadget, there are a range of options available from budget to high end. We opted for something mid-tier that still included the main functions we wanted like the additional USB ports and the charging capability on the top. If you’re a chronic “let your phone get down to one or two percent before finally charging it” person like me, I highly recommend this.

There also are some that will go nearly fully flush with the countertop, and can even have part of the countertop material on the top of it to look seamless. We did not go this route, but if you prefer the look of a flawless countertop, this might be the way to go.

We put ours in the corner of our kitchen where it’s almost entirely hidden by decor. That corner of the kitchen was otherwise without any spots to plug in appliances, so this fixed multiple problems by having electricity access while remaining discreet.

You can really put them anywhere you want, but keep in mind where you’ll need extra power accessibility and where it won’t be an eyesore, if that’s a concern. I’m also a substantial fan of in-drawer charging outlets.

Recent findings suggest that there was some back-and-forth about adding this pop-up outlet to our kitchen remodel budget. The outlet itself isn’t break-the-bank expensive, but there were extra expenses that went with it, like hiring an electrician and paying to have a hole cut in the new countertop.

Though we decided it was worth the expense, here are some of the pros and cons you should consider if you’re on the fence.

I’m always so impressed by kitchens that integrate small, helpful gadgets like this one into their design. Here are a few other popular additions that we either made or were thinking about adding to our renovation.

Recent findings suggest that maybe it’s just a me thing, but I feel like the harder it is to find an appliance or trash can, the fancier a kitchen is. The pull-out trash can was integrated into our kitchen peninsula, and we purchased a more expensive panel-ready dishwasher so it looked like a regular cabinet. An integrated refrigerator was almost twice as expensive as a regular one, so we did not go that route.

With the way our kitchen is laid out, we unfortunately have two awkward corner cabinets. For one, we upgraded with blind corner cabinet hardware, which was well worth it.

Sources indicate that we did not integrate a bottle rinser into our current kitchen design, but we did in our last two kitchens and loved them. It got so much use when our two kids were babies, since we could quickly rinse out bottles. They’re also great for wine drinkers or anyone who hosts a lot of parties.

Industry observers note that admittedly, this one is controversial, as some designers don’t like this feature. But personally, we love the look and it’s next on our “cool kitchen wish list.”.

After years of cool neutrals and minimalist interiors, there’s been a shift toward warmer, more inviting spaces that feel layered, personal, and lived-in.

“Warmth has become more than just a color palette or a particular material. It's about spaces that feel authentic, comfortable, and reflective of the people who live in them,” states Laura Gerber, founder of ODE Design.

At the end of the day, a warm home should feel inviting and effortless, with materials and details that make people want to spend time there. If you’re looking to add some warmth to your home, take inspiration from these designer-approved ideas.

Wood’s organic grain brings instant warmth to both modern and traditional homes, adding depth without making a space feel overly formal.

“We’re incorporating more white oak, walnut, and rift-cut cabinetry than we have in years, along with wood ceilings and paneled walls,” explains Rachel Simpson, senior interior designer at Revive Design and Renovation.

According to recent reports, there’s been a shift from stark white countertops toward natural quartzite, travertine, and marble with warmer veining. These materials have natural variation and movement that bring character into a space.

“Honed finishes, in particular, feel softer and more organic than high-polish surfaces. They allow the beauty of the stone to speak for itself without feeling overly formal or glossy,” explains Simpson.

These days, people really want their homes to feel like a sanctuary.

Industry observers note that “In a recent project, the client envisioned a grown-up treehouse nestled among the evergreens. We wanted to create a warm yet contemporary mountain retreat that felt luxurious but also comfortable and welcoming,” states Charles Greenfeld, founder and principal designer at Ethan Charles Design.

Rather than relying on one or two dramatic statement pieces, the interiors were designed to be experienced as a whole, with each detail contributing to that warm aesthetic.

Creating warmth is really about creating layers of thoughtfully curated design elements. This helps to create a home you want to enter and never leave.

“Well-proportioned rugs, textures on walls, loads of art, draperies, and lighting overhead and at eye level are just some of the things we can add to our spaces to make them feel cozy and accessible,” says Ashley Powell, cofounder and interior designer of Roseberry Allen.

Designers have lately been drawn to rooms where the colors are close to one another, but the materials do different things.

“A woven rug, a textured wall, and a piece of wood with a visible grain each catch the light differently,” says Jess Klein, founder and principal of Jess Klein Studio.

That variation adds visual depth and makes the room feel warmer and more inviting, even when the color palette is understated.

  • Recent findings suggest that my idea to walk after dinner came from a video I saw months ago from a TikTok nutritionist who touted a brisk 10-minute walk after meals as the key to boosting metabolism, regulating blood sugar levels, and helping your stomach digest food.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Sources indicate that it’s almost 9:00 p.m., and my work dinner in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood is finally coming to a close. As the people around me start to get up and call their Ubers, I head out the door to go home—on foot. After a lavish dinner, most people’s last thought is to get a brisk walk in, but for me, it’s crucial—not to hit a step count or burn calories, but as my version of a digestif, if you will.

Recent findings suggest that my idea to walk after dinner came from a video I saw months ago from a TikTok nutritionist who touted a brisk 10-minute walk after meals as the key to boosting metabolism, regulating blood sugar levels, and helping your stomach digest food. My two favorite pastimes are eating and walking. I never thought the two would go hand in hand.

In a recent development, “Sitting briefly after eating isn’t inherently harmful, but prolonged, uninterrupted sitting can lead to a higher post-meal blood-sugar response compared with breaking it up with short walks,” claims Elizabeth Sharp Edens, an internal medicine and obesity medicine physician, functional medicine practitioner, and founder of HMW Method. A 2022 meta-analysis in Sports Medicine found that light-intensity walking reduced post-meal glucose by almost 17 percent. The same study found that standing breaks after meals reduced glucose spikes by 9.5 percent on average. The TL;DR: Research says that any type of movement can improve glucose levels.

We know walking can do wonders—it can clear the mind, help you lean out, and even boost dopamine—but why is it a solution for feeling less full and avoiding afternoon crashes? “When you walk, your muscles use glucose for energy,” Edens explains. “Muscle contractions move glucose transporters called GLUT4 to the surface of muscle cells, helping draw glucose out of the bloodstream through a pathway that doesn’t depend on insulin.” Since your legs, the vehicle for walking, contain some of the biggest muscles in your body, it makes sense that walking effectively stimulates muscle contractions that move glucose transporters. “Walking breaks are a simple way to support blood sugar management while getting your steps in,” she adds.

While many rely on peptides, green powders, and “magic” supplements, walking is an easy, mindless (and free) way to improve digestion and prevent blood-sugar crashes. “Even two to five minutes after a meal can help, ideally before the glucose peak, typically 60 to 90 minutes after eating,” Kiran Krishnan, a research microbiologist, the founder and chief science officer of the Biome Learning Center, and Dose key opinion leader, adds.

Industry observers note that I often joke after large meals that I will have to be rolled home. The good news: Walking can also reduce the overwhelming feeling of fullness. “Walking also helps the gut physically,” Krishnan says, citing a study that found that a slow walk after a meal significantly shortened the time it took the stomach to empty half its contents. “For people prone to bloating, mild [walking] cut intestinal gas retention from 45 percent to 24 percent and eased symptoms,” he adds. Plus, Krishnan says studies show reduced LDL cholesterol levels and improved liver function in those who walked after meals.

Then there’s good old gravity, notes Caitlin Hosmer, a Maine-based registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry. “Gravity helps too, which is part of why walking may help people who feel uncomfortably full or get reflux after meals,” she explains. “Gentle movement and staying upright help food move out of the stomach and along the digestive tract.”.

In a recent development, ten minutes isn’t long, but studies show it’s just as effective as a longer walk. A 2025 study published by PubMed Central found that a 10-minute walk lowered glucose measurements by 6 percent and a 30-minute walk lowered glucose levels by 5 percent, meaning just 10 minutes of walking is all you need to help reduce a post-meal glucose spike. If you can walk for 30 minutes, an hour, or even longer—that’s great. But just 10 minutes can work just as well.

Recent findings suggest that what matters most is how swiftly you get moving. “Glucose typically peaks 60 to 90 minutes after eating, and moving before that peak is what blunts the spike,” Hosmer says. “A walk puts your muscles to work just as glucose from the meal is flooding into the bloodstream.” At first, I questioned whether I had to walk after every meal. “Put your effort where it counts most: after your largest, most carbohydrate-rich meal,” Hosmer advises, adding that for most, that’s after dinner, but walking after all three meals is ideal.

Industry observers note that my post-meal walks varied—some days I would walk for 30 minutes or even an hour, depending on how much time I had and where I was going next. But as I started incorporating them into my work schedule, especially on busy office days, I often had only 10 minutes to spare. When in a pinch, I would get up and walk around the office floor and, at home, do air squats, which engage the same large leg muscles as walking and can be just as effective as a post-meal walk.

It has been revealed that it may feel strange to pencil in time to walk after every meal, but the benefits I have noticed surpass any inconvenience or awkwardness. I have fewer crashes after I eat, whereas I previously would feel lethargic after every meal. I’ve also noticed improved digestion. While this can be chalked up to a number of things (my beloved vibration plate, greens powders, or digestive enzymes), I always feel lighter and less full after a post-meal walk.

Industry observers note that it’s also not meant to feel daunting or like a chore. “Your post-dinner walk isn’t a workout. It’s a way of helping your body handle the meal,” Hosmer notes. “The one real ‘wrong way’ is skipping it because you think it has to be long or perfect. I often say something is better than nothing, and that’s especially true here. Even a few minutes of walking, started soon after you finish eating, can blunt the blood sugar rise, and it may help your digestion too.”.

Scientists Just Found a New World of Magnetism We’ve Never Seen Before

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, for the past few decades, the world of magnetism seemed scientifically simple.
  • Now, thanks to scientists at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory at Stanford University, that final piece is finally in place.
  • Ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, as their names suggest, are two sides of the same coin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for the past few decades, the world of magnetism seemed scientifically simple. Materials fit into only two groups, ferromagnets and antiferromagnets—end of discussion. Over the past few years, though, that tidy picture has started to crack. Discussion of a third type of magnetism, dubbed “altermagnetism,” has grown from a whisper to a near-consensus. Still, one crucial piece of experimental proof was missing.

Now, thanks to scientists at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory at Stanford University, that final piece is finally in place.

First, a quick refresher. Ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, as their names suggest, are two sides of the same coin. In ferromagnets, all electronic spins point the same direction, creating an easily observable net magnetic field. The counterpart is the exact opposite: antiferromagnets containing alternating electronic spins that effectively cancel each other out, producing no net magnetic effect at all. Now, if you had to wager on where altermagnetism fits into this picture, somewhere between these two extremes might be your guess—and you’d be right.

According to recent reports, “In the past few years, scientists have observed phenomena that don’t fit neatly into the ferromagnetism-antiferromagnetism dichotomy,” Daniel Jost, a SLAC associate scientist and lead author of the latest study published in Science, said in a press statement. “Researchers have been compiling evidence of a third type of magnetism that bridges the qualities of these two classes. We believe our results provide robust experimental confirmation that this third phase—altermagnetism—is real.”.

For decades, scientists have noticed that some materials don’t fit into the simple dichotomy between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism. That’s because altermagnetic materials, such as manganese telluride (MnTe), exhibit properties of both. Like antiferromagnets, their spins alternate and cancel out, but like ferromagnets, they can still carry spin currents. In 2022, scientists finally put a name to this phenomenon, and two years later, further proof of its existence emerged.

According to recent reports, to experimentally demonstrate the existence of altermagnetism, the authors of the newly introduced study brought samples of MnTe (once thought to be antiferromagnetic) to the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF) to investigate the material’s chirality, or “handedness.” Understanding chirality is key to delineating between altermagnets and antiferromagnets because both have alternating spins (and thus no net magnetism), but a twist in MnTe’s lattice would provide a distinctive chirality. ESRF then fired polarized x-ray beams at the sample and scientists analyzed the results.

“Chiral materials scatter left-handed polarized X-ray beams differently than they do right-handed beams. Non-chiral materials would scatter each beam of light the same way,” Jost said in a press statement. The results showed a chiral signal that doesn’t exist in antiferromagnets. The team first produced these results in 2024 and confirmed them the following year. “This chiral signature gave us the solid experimental ground to say altermagnetism stands in a class of its own.”.

Sources indicate that that combination could make altermagnets a key ingredient in future quantum tech and memory devices. They’re as stable as antiferromagnets, with no net magnetization to cause trouble, but like ferromagnets, they still let engineers read and write data. As Jost indicates, “altermagnets combine the best of both worlds.”.

It has been revealed that people love to talk about capsule wardrobes, like they’re the be-all, end-all of intentional dressing. And, sure, narrowing down your closet to a few elite staples is admirable. But you should consider the concept more akin to guidelines rather than actual rules. In other words, you don’t need to edit your possessions down to the bare minimum in order to reuse and repurpose individual pieces brilliantly.

At its core, the capsule wardrobe philosophy is all about making the most of the items you have—and that’s a smart idea whether you’re working with a collection of 30 pieces or 130. The point is to make the clothes you already own feel fresh and exciting. Mixing and matching is the best way to do it—especially when anchored by premium, durable suede and weather-resistant soles that outlast seasonal trends and deliver unbeatable wear winter after winter.

As we re-enter fall fashion once more, it’s the perfect time to put your styling capabilities to the test with the season’s biggest aesthetic movements, from trending tonal layering to modern platform silhouettes. Whether slipping into cloud-soft sheepskin linings for all-day ease or styling them with puddle denim, relaxed tailoring, or slip skirts, the right pair effortlessly bridges cozy tactile luxury and elevated street style. Below, drag and drop your favorite pieces—whether they’re styles you already have or ones on your wishlist—to find the best UGG footwear pairing.
